A couple years ago I bought the RC Disc version for my laptop, I loved it so much that when the humble bundle star wars came around I paid 15.00 bucks without even looking at the other games. Now this game like any other has its flaws, graphics have become outdated although not horendous. Enemy AI is predictable and doesn't vary alot. Squadmate AI leads to constant friendly fire when you are between them and a target. And finally, and most dissappiontingly to me, a fairly short story. But the things it is good at, it is great at, compelling squadmates who even though the fit simplistic categories are still intresting and always have a few jokes on hand (except Fixer, he's a party pooper). Easy squad controls that are still effective in any situation. You can be a tank if you want on easy mode or a glass window with a target spray painted on in hard mode (Even a regular enemy can take you down to low health in a 1vs. 1). The health system makes every battle have lasting effects but you still regen health. Shields come back auto. but reg. health needs a med station. This game used to have multi-player but that went off a year or two ago, no co-op which seems like an obvious thing. Lightly-destructable enviorments, (tanks destroy stuff and demo charges can be placed at certain spots).
Boss-38 (You): Level headed, logically thinking, no nonsense seageant.
Fixer-40 (Hacker/2nd in Command): Follows the book to the letter, not a bad guy but could probably ease up a little ;-).
Scorch-62(Demolitions Expert/Jokester): Always has a joke loaded and ready to fire, enjoys making fun of Sev and Fixer.
Sev-07(Sniper): "Sev: Some people say that in order to achieve maximum combat effectiveness, they need to get into the zone. Sir, I *live* in the zone." 'nough said.
To finish up, while the short campagian means that you may only get a few hours out of this game if you don't want to replay it, I think this game has enough replay value if you try new things yourself instead of waiting for the game to do new things. Just to show I mean that, I at the time of this review have played RC for 44 hours according to Steam, if you divide that by the $15 I spent on the previously mentioned Humble Bundle then I paid about 33-34 cents per hour, as a person who loves Star Wars, I still am not to the point where I'm at that kind of ratio with even my favorite of the movies.

Armello is an interesting game with some fun mechanics.
That being said, it really doesn't live up to my expectations.
The user interface is somewhat clunky.  There isn't a summary screen of how you stack up to your opponents, and it's quite easy to accidentally move your character when wanting to exit your inventory screen.
The other big issue that I have with Armello is that there is no way to skip animations, and this ends up slowing down gameplay considerably.  I don't need to see the 5 second animation of the king being injured or gaining bane (or whatever it's called).  Basically, streamlining the whole thing would be good, and make me feel like the game isn't wasting my time.
The game is built something like a board game, so I would also expect there to be a "quick move" option (skip walking animations, item animations, etc.).
The last issue I have is that you have to pay to unlock different characters.  Frankly, it's simply an unpleasant aspect of the game and something of a turn-off to most people.  Make the other characters part of a DLC, or provide some way for people who are happy to grind for weeks to have access to these characters, items, etc.
In any case, it's a reasonably fun game for ~ 5-10 hours, but after that the issues mentioned above become increasingly apparent.

As a gamer, I generally have a good feel for which games I will find fun and which I will wish I had never bought.  Any game with a good plot usually falls into the former category for me, regardless of the genre.  And while I like FPS games in general, I never bothered with games like Call of Duty, which were, in my opinion, shooting solely for the sake of shooting.  So, when someone gifted me Battlefield: Bad Company 2 on Steam, I decided I might as well give it a try.
To begin with, I will give the developers credit for integrating the tutorial with the opening mission, and at the same time, not turning it into a “tutorial mission."  Learning the controls was integrated well with the mission, and I didn’t feel like the mission was custom-tailored to teaching me.
The plot however, was exactly as I expected: a mildly-coherent excuse for more shooting.  I vaguely remember something about the Russians having some evil doomsday weapon (which sounded like some kind of giant EMP generator) and my squad somehow being the only ones qualified to stop/find/destroy it.  And it being excuse for more shooting, the plot must always take the route of greatest enemy contact.  I found the weapon once, but of course it was only a fake weapon, and I then had to go to South America and kill some local militia-folk in order to find the real one.
As the plot is usually my principal motivator in FPS games, I quickly grew frustrated with my plot-to-death ratio playing on the Normal difficulty.  I had one mission where I had to make my way down a mountain in a blizzard, and not only did I have to avoid bullets and RPGs, but I had to avoid dying of hypothermia by taking shelter in strategically placed small homes.  I eventually got to a bridge with scores of Russians on the other side, and I could not, for the life of me, make it across without either dying from being shot too many times or dying from hypothermia by staying in my cover too long.  It was at this point that I got fed up and switched to the Easy difficulty.  After doing so, the rate at which I was dying became far more tolerable for the relatively ♥♥♥♥♥♥ plot I was being served.
Overall, I don’t know if I can say that Battlefield: Bad Company 2 is a bad game, but I do know that it’s not for me.  The plot is completely token, I die way too often, and even on Easy difficulty there’s too much shooting and not enough plot-advancing for my tastes.
P.S.: If you want to hear more about Battlefield: Bad Company 2, along with some of the other gripes I had with it, check out Yahtzee’s Zero Punctuation
about the game (he’s just about as fed up with realistic cover-based shooters as I am).

Card Hunter is perhaps the best free to play RPG  online today.   It has a fun premise: you are playing a new RPG on a table in a friend's basement. His older brother who owns the game pops in to bug you now and then.  You may even get visited by the cute pizza delivery girl and get to watch your friend get all flustered. :)  The game itself is a cool blend of CCG (collectible card game) and minis based tactical RPG. It reminds me a bit of D&D's Dungeon Command game in that what you can make the heroes in your adventuring party do depends on the cards you draw from your deck at the start of each round.  It has all the traditional trappings of a classic RPG with wizards, clerics, fighters, monsters etc. plus it has fun twists on spells, items and abilities.  The sound effects, graphics and user interface all combine to really put you in the folding chair seat of the setting. It's metagaming in the best sense of the word.  The A.I. that runs Gary (your friend in the solo game) is competent once you get into the game a bit and he's shown you how to play. Then, he gets a bit tougher as he runs the monsters, traps etc.  The game gradually unfolds with new areas, equipment, abilites etc. so that you aren't overwhelmed with learning how to play it and there's a nice sense of progression.  You can also play multiplayer with other people.  This works well as long as everyone has a high speed connection. This seems like a nice concept: Hack-n-Slash game with community content and custom dungeons and LOOTING!!!! So what we look for in this game is how fun it is to LOOT, how fun the classes and their development is and how good the combat feels. Let's see how it fares. In those 3 aspects.
Looting in this game seemed quite decent. I mean you get frequent chests, you get monster drops and "higher-value" chests and also something like a "boss"-drops. The system where you can "donate" junk and gold to shrine to "pray" for random good items for various slots is also a nice gamble and adds to all of the Gearing up aspect of an Hack-n-Slash.
The combat is where the game falls flat and by a huge margin. By no means is combat any fun. The hit detection is abysmal. I feel this game has worse or more difficult combat than Dark Souls for PC and that game aims to be difficult and challenging.  Half the time you will be missing the enemy because you're not facing them, that's okay... half of the time when you are facing the enemy you still won't hit it, because your cursor is slightly off! Now even with everything angled right the hit-boxes are drunk and sway around the actual model.
The classes... You have 4 classes ( 2 mages, a warrior and a semi-warrior )... All of whom mostly swing their prefered weapon, at least at the early levels. Now I want you to pick ANY 4 heroes/champions/classes from an MOBA game and imagine having a GRINDING RPG game built around them... you have 4 abilities that hardly ever improve or feel different for all of the gear grinding and loot farming. I said 4? Yes that is if you play with each and seperate one, but mostly you'll be stuck with ONE.
I might have a bit biased oppinion, but that's what this god-awful combat system got me to. I have few reviews and generally prefer to write pleasant and good ones about games I like, but for me to write a negative one, the game seriously must SUCK.
I understand that the game is popular amongst some of you people, but so is Minecraft... and hell if I knew why..

Well let's start out with the good. The rendered 2D World is absolutely beautiful. A lot of vibrant colours, whimsical looking enemies. Oozi is very reminiscent of games like Rayman Origins and Legends. A very cartoon like visual that's fun and eye pleasing. The animations do not feel completely fluid, however, that does not mean it detracts from the rest of the visuals.
Each new world is pleasant and visually pleasing, each one different from the last to keep you entertained. The game offers a plethora of visual cues to warn the player of an incoming and/or timed trap. I never felt like the game was trying to pull a fast one and sneak in a random kill on me.
The platforming mechanics are solid with tight controls. Oozi never felt sluggish when jumping or turning. Any time I missed a jump or fell it felt like it was my fault by dropping an input or jumping too soon. Being able to chain multiple jumps and bouncing off opponents just feels so natural in this game. One jump to the next is fluid, mid air turns are quick and responsive. Oozi does feel a little floaty while jumping, but I don't feel this is a problem with the mechanics and most of the time it was advantatious to use this floatiness.
The only complaint I have with the mechanics is the Wall Jumping, it's very clunky and slow. I found it can be incredibly frustrating to deal with. Perhaps I've been spoiled by other platformers that feature wall jumping, but I just can't dismiss this. All in all the mechanics are solid though and wall Jumping is just a small part of the entire game.
The game has four different difficulty modes ranging from Kid to Hardcore. Higher difficulty modes typically add more enemies, lower Oozi's life hearts by one and adds more traps to each level. Kid mode is unique in that Oozi has a much higher jump. While the game is certainly never difficult to the point you want to tear your hair out it never claims to be that way. If you're looking for a Super Meat Boy difficult then it's probably best to avoid this game. If you want a fun and relaxing platforming experience that can some of the time offer a difficult challenge then look no more.
The game features three game modes. A Main story that follows Oozi in the search of his lost spacesuit and spaceship. Each level is followed up by a cute comic describing his adventures and to provide some semblance of a plot. As you progress the main story you unlock new abilities for Oozi such as the ability to Wall Jump or "Pound" Enemies. This kept things slightly more fresh as you progress and adds more elements to the platforming experience. While the levels can be fairly long the game offers plentiful amount of checkpoints in case of screwups. Each world has its own unique boss that are pattern based and felt slightly on the easy side. This isn't exactly a huge problem, but I would have liked to see more random elements added to bosses.
The second mode is the Challenge Mode. Challenge mode presents you with a variety of challenges ranging from something as easy as Completing the level to killing a specific set of opponents. There are also a variety of bonus challenges within each level to add a layer of difficulty to further challenge the player. Arcade Mode is the third and final mode. It offers a timed checkpoint based challenge. The main objective is to complete the level with as many points as possible and not dying the entire way. You do earn health through so missed jumps or damage skips are possible to save time. There is a bunch of bonus content to keep you interested. I feel there might be slightly too many challenge levels, but that's just a personal opinion on that.
Oozi: Earth Adventure offers a great platforming experience for any fan of the genre. It harkens back to the day of old school platforming where mechanics were solid and tight. It doesn't try to be more than that, but I don't believe the developers are trying to be different. Oozi offers a refined platforming experience many of us grew up with. I can't help but recommend this game to anyone who's a fan of platformers.
Pros:
- Great Visuals and easy to navigate menus.
- Refined Classic Platforming Experience.
- Fairly good music that fits the games aesthetics.
- Great Value for a lot of content.
Cons:
- Some clunky mechanics like Wall Jumping.
- Bosses feel too predictable.
- Some levels feel too long even with checkpoints.
- Occasional Crashing.

Full review:
Oozi: Earth Adventure is a platforming game characterized by its classic platforming mechanics, back when puzzles and punishment in platformers did not really play a major role in the gameplay. This is how the game is officially described and although it does fit the description well, it does have a few flaws that certainly take away from the experience
Essentially, Oozi: Earth Adventure is just straight-up platforming. No gimmicks, just platforms. This did appeal to me before I started playing it, but then I realized how repetitive that could become. The gameplay itself is relatively simple, as that is how the game is advertised. It does have all of the platforming basics, movement, jumping, moving platforms, gaping holes, etc. There are also enemies that can be destroyed in a variety of ways, depending on the type of enemy. Usually, enemies are destroyed simply by jumping onto them, Mario-style, but some can only be killed by a ground-pound and some just cannot be killed.
You also have your basic platforming obstacles, like moving platforms, spike traps, lava pits, etc. Very basic features. The game adds little to differentiate itself from other platformers, but I do tend to review games based on what they are, instead of what they're not, and this game is advertised as a classical platformer anyways. This would certainly appeal to platforming fans looking for a simple, laid-back experience that takes about four hours to beat. The game also features amazing visuals, as well as amazing music. The music is very fitting to its corresponding world, with each world having its own personality.
The world and level design is well-executed, each world having its own special set enemies, obstacles, music, etc. I really enjoyed the third world, which was inside a laboratory with bright white walls and radioactive waste everywhere. The gameplay can become repetitive at parts, especially when you get stuck at one checkpoint and end up dying a dozen times trying to reach the next checkpoint. Most of the checkpoints in the game were reasonably placed, but a few were placed a little too far out, causing me much frustration as I died repeatedly just trying to reach said checkpoint. I would sometimes die a few steps from the checkpoint and have to redo my whole run from the previous checkpoint, which I found very aggravating.
The game seems to be lacking in replayability, however. The only reason I can see someone replaying this is to get a higher score for a higher position on the leaderboards (which I placed 13th in after I beat the game) or to collect the hidden stars in each level, which unlock more stages to play, like challenge and arcade stages. The challenge stages were simply the same as their corresponding stage, just with a few extra objectives, like not taking damage, or beating it in a certain time.
Overall, Oozi: Earth Adventure can find its true audience in those looking for a simplistic platforming experience. Although the game has limited mechanics and repetitive gameplay, it's still a new experience that platforming fans can take up just for the fun of it. Oh, I'd also like to point out Oozi's smile. Just look at that! The corners of his mouth GOES ABOVE HIS EYES.

Do you like the Fallout stories and world? Do you enjoy big guns and making mutants go boom?  Then this game might be for you if you are down for running a 6 man (or woman or mixed) team of soldiers in retaking the wasteland from the Mutants, ghouls, raiders and other enemies you meet along the way!
This game uses a large over world map that you can freely explore (ahla Fallout 1 and 2) and run into random encounters or just plot a point to your next objective.  Once you hit an encounter or your next objective it changes over to a 3/4th top down view of the battlefield and gives you command of your troopers.  You can either run the game in real time or in turn based (as in Fallout 1 and 2).  I've found the game much more enjoyable in the real time element.  You can for instance have a sniper climb a tower to spot enemies, then sneak a couple of other people up to either side of a door and set them to fire on anything that comes rushing out.  Once the sniper takes the first shot it's game on.
Honestly the reviews when the game came out largely panned the game but I feel like it deserves better than it got.  This is one of my favorite games.   If you like Final Fantasy Tactics or Jagged Alliance or are just a hard core Fallout fan this game is more than likely something you would enjoy.  Or as another endorsement I still own my disc copy of this game from when it came out, but I went ahead and bought it again on Steam just for convience.

This game had one thing and ONLY one thing going for it. That was the fact that they brought in a writer and several voice actors from the Clone Wars cartoon. So the atmophere of the game is a flawless imitation of the Clone Wars cartoon. The characterization is dead on to fans of the show (including, true to the cartoon's form, the snarkiest Obi-Wan Kenobi ever to be seen in any fictional work). The story isn't
per se, but it certainly feels like an odd playable episode of the television show, which allowed me to hate it less than it deserves to be hated.
After a nice opening cutscene, it all goes downhill fast when you're given control for the first time, and you spend five minutes trying to find, learn, and understand the ludicrous controls. As you're learning you are assaulted with poor graphics, unexciting combat, bland levels, poor camera angles, and possibly the worst platforming I have seen in any game ever - certainly the worst in any 21st century game. Further, I started the game controlling both characters at once (multiplayer mode), which was incredibly ungainly, and the rest of the game was so bad that I assumed this was just part of the awfulness and slogged through the first hour of the game trying to play one character with each hand. It got so annoying eventually that I googled around and saw that oh, there was a single player option that the menus made absolutely no effort to direct me to.
If you got this as part of the Star Wars package, you can safely skip it unless you're a Clone Wars superfan. If you're considering buying it by itself, save yourself a headache and don't.

Lock and load, because it's about to get bad company. This is by far the best Battlefield game in my option. EA Dice did an amazing job with the graphic, guns, gameplay and a great solid campaign. I didn't get to play the first game but I did play a few minute with the campaign. Battlefield is supposed to be a contender to CoD which to me seem to obscure. Both games are different either way, and no matter how hard you compare them, they're all different in term of gameplay element.
Gameplay:
The gameplay feel nice and fluent. The map are well made and well design, my favorite one so far are Oais and Heavy Metal. The campaign continue with the bad company , the story is rock solid and it's by far the best in the series. The multiplayer is the main reason I brought the game, the teamwork involve, the vehicle, and the lovely destruction in this game. No wonder Battlefield bad company 2 is the best. Unlike Battlefield 4 levelution, Bad Company 2 destruction feel dynamic. I don't like it when that one jerk decided to flood an entire map and force me into fighting onto the rooftop and get killed by an enemy boats and helicopters. 32 players is enough to cause some mayhem and destruction in the game. One thing that I hate about bad company 2 is how you have to unlocked the febulator and the ammo boxes. They are essential to the game element of teamwork! Other than that, the game is amazing and makes you feel like you're in a battlefield. If you're bored of the modern setting, there's always the Vietnam DLC which is more than a reskin, it felt like a whole new game.
Graphic:
Running on the FrostBite 1 engine, the game is gourges in evryway while maintains beutiful, solid framrate! I remember when EA launch BF4, my PC was having hard time running that broken piece of crap until it took a lot of patches to fix the danm game. BF bad company 2 sounds effects are amazing. The frostbite engine did an excellent job of making destruction, don't get me wrong I love BF4 levelution, but it felt kind of scripted. An enemy behind a cover? Just shoot a 40mm grenade at it, you're not sure if there's enemy in a building, just destroy it with a tank. Punch a hole in a wall. Or break down fences that is in your way. The shaders are also note worthy. Not only the texture and the sound of the game's amazing but the shaders of the frostbite engine is infomous for making Battlefield look like a geniue masterpiece. Lighting is good and the shadows is good, if you're worry about any graphic loss cuz this game still look good on low setting.
Verdict:
Is it worth it? Yes! It's fun, chaotic, and the campaign is rock solid. I would love a Bad Company 3 next year, or maybe a Vietnam sequal.

This may seem like an exaggeration, but Star Wars: Republic Commando may be the best game I've ever played. I am a huge Star Wars fan, and I actually found out about this game from the
. I bought this game during a sale and mostly left it alone until recently. Now, after playing it for a few hours, I can confirm that it is everything that its small but fanatic cult following says it is.
This depiction of the Star Wars universe is much darker than any other I've encountered before. Rather than following the heroic Jedi in an unrealistic "good vs evil" fight, Republic Commandos occupy that "gray area" and win their fights through brutal efficiency. In fact, Jedi don't even play a significant role in this game. Also, rather than showing typical sanitized Star Wars death (no blood), gratuitous amounts of gore frequently splatters the player's helmet (yay), which is eventually cleaned by a nifty windshield wiper-like device.
Gameplay is heavily centered around a squad of four, where the leader is controlled by the player. Commands are given to the other three soldiers, consisting of a sniper, a demolitions expert, and a hacker. AI teammates are actually useful in this game without making it too easy for the player (take notes, Overkill). Each member can be told to perform certain tasks, such as manning a turret, blowing a door open, or providing sniper fire. Everything feels seamless and well-executed, especially the
. #SquadGoals
Graphics are, well, 2005. Can't expect much. The resolution doesn't even go to 1080p. Thankfully, there are mods to fix that. They're good enough to create a reasonably immersive environment, but I'd like to think that it's the story and gameplay that makes this game what it is. The soundtrack fills in the rest of the atmosphere, which is a combination of John Williams glory and some original compositions. Good music is pretty much a given for anything Star Wars related.
About the story (SPOILERS AHEAD):
TL;DR: Underrated squad-based first person shooter with great mechanics and story. Give sequel pls

Edit: Something I just have to add in is that after you finish the first campaign, the second one starts throwing out RNG REALLY HARD. My enjoyment of the game plummeted on the first level as I literally had to just keep smashing my face against each encounter due to terrible RNG throwing out any chance I had. Got a card that next turn will win you the game? That's nice, RADIATION! Bye bye card. Wouldn't be so bad if there were cards to protect against it or if things were more predictable, but this really just killed my enjoyment for the game hard.
With this game I was initially surprised by how much I was enjoying it. Pulled in by the strangely endearing Gary character and his seemingly elitest brother Melvin. The card system itself was really nice and I was always eager to see what set of cards I'd draw each turn and see how I'd use them. Honestly the basic mechanics of the game itself are really nice for what it is, although a tad too heavy on the RNG even for someone like myself who rather enjoys that sort of thing. I really only found the RNG to be annoying and it never truly crossed into obnoxious territory, but it certainly would have helped to have a little more strategy and predictability than is offered. Holding over 2 cards is nice...but it was pretty rare for me to find myself trying to decide between cards and most of the time just shredding extra move cards or just 'the weaker' of two.
Don't get me wrong I'm glad there is 'SOME' predictability, but it does roll into annoying territory that you don't get the choice of 'gauranteeing' a card type each turn or something of the sort since sometimes I'd have a hand full of move cards, toss most of em and then next turn pull even more god damned move cards. There should be a flex system to allow you to pick at the end of each turn for each character what card you want to gaurantee you will pull. That would satisfy me personally and rid me of the sighs.
Theres mostly adventures with your party that you build up over time and they're all pretty enjoyable. You can even co op with friends (though the system needs to allow 2 players to get 3 party members. That's stupid that you can't.). I also feel like I'd be a little happier with a fourth class and fourth character slot, but I'm ok if it doesn't have it. Guess this is as good as any place to mention there are elves and that just makes me happy. Wish you could change the damn color schemes to them though. I seen alternate color schemes so I know they exist, but I'm guessing they're only for special encounters or pvp.
Also I don't like the 'custom adventures'. I think some of them are horrendously imbalanced and designed. They wouldn't be anywhere near as frustrating if they were 'one offs' but most of them are groups of them, like 3 at a time and in order to get through them you have to do them all in one swoop. It works fine and dandy when it's YOUR PARTY and you can adjust your characters to suit the encounter, but not in special challenges where you're essentially figuring out a puzzle. Beat the first two and stuck trying to figure out how to beat the last one? Well ♥♥♥♥ you. This whole 'win 3 in a row' really hurts the game badly especially with specialty puzzle encounters where figuring out the puzzle means that anytime you have to redo it, it's just going through the motions again.
I know before I said that I liked Gary and Melvin, but I do have to say that the two started to wear on me a bit down the line with both of them being a little too stereotypical for my tastes. I guess the 'childlike wonder' effect wore off on me a little early though so I wouldn't take my word on it. I might be a little too chiseled around the edges know what I mean?
So you must be wondering why the review SEEMS so positive, but is negative right? Well I can't in good conscience give a game with gambling and P2W a good review. Sorry. The game has online vs and it's based on buildable characters and items that you can buy with 'pizza slices' (awesome premium currency name btw). I'm totally down with omitting 'adventures' as paid content, that's fine. This game really feels pretty heavy on singleplayer too so yah. Unfortunately since you can pay real money to buy 'chests' that will give gear I can't give it a positive review. I ain't down with that. It makes it worse that there is pvp too.
In the end though it's actually a pretty cool game and I think I will play it more. I mean up until I get really frustrated with the RNG or some♥♥♥♥♥♥ If you got the time though you should probably at least check it out. Couldn't hurt right? It's F2P as they say.

I've played Dungeons and Dragons in some form for pretty much my entire life, before I knew the official rules and had the friends to play (about 6-7 years old) I'd actually make my own version based on stories my dad and uncle would tell me about when they played in high school. Eventually I got older and bought my own copy of the DM Guide and Players Handbook and would play with friends. This game captures both of those experiences. But what really makes me enjoy the game more is the little details they add that only a true dice rolling dungeoneer would know about (the older brother yelling at you for using his characters and then mocking of your campaign or calling the same pizza place over and over to get the cute girl delivery but being afraid to talk to her, and many others)
The card based combat system is very easy to pick up, but it takes a little bit longer to develop proper tactics based on your deck. If you are looking for a card game like Magic the Gathering then this is not for you, but if you have ever played Dungeons and Dragons or any other pen and paper style role playing game then I recommend trying it out for a little bit.

"A Game of Thrones, only with animals" they said.
Haven't heard this much bull***t since the day my ex-girlfriend told me we'd be together forever.
Let me paint you a picture what this game is:
>You pick yourself a Rat to grab some easy monies from nearby settlements.
>You grab a might amulet so you don't die in combat too fast
>You start the match
>Your enemies have like 3 settlements, 2 dungeons and a healing circle spawn around their bases among the forests and fields.
>You get a Mountain range spanning 3 nearby slots, 2 swamps and a dungeon.
>You enter the dungeon hoping for some gold.
>You encounter a 3 symbols peril, you have 4 dice and 4 cards.
>You burn 2 cards for 2 symbols
>You throw your other dice hoping to get a shield.
>Moon and Rot
>You get teleported to the furthest dungeon on the map
>As you watch the scavenge roll you hope for some juicy gold from it
>You rolled teleport, you teleport back to your dungeon
>Enjoy your first turn
>Hop a bit further into the game
>You encounter a Bane in the dungeon and get attacked
>No matter you're stocked up like Charlie Sheen's dealer on Christmas Eve
>Let the fight begin, you have 8 dice + 2 bonus attack and defense from items, Bane's got 4 dice
>What could possibly go wrong?
>You roll a Rot 6 times, end up with 2 attack and 4 defense
>Bane begins his explosive chain, his 4 dice multiply until he gets 12 attack and 2 defense
>You watch yourself poking at the Bird of Darkness with a toothpick
>You turn around, lay down and spread your buttcheeks
>Bane ravages your insides with his mighty 12 inches worth of attack power.
>Then Wolfie McNutNugget decides to attack the Lion King
>He barely deals some damage to him but hey, he's at one health after like 5 rounds so it's okay
>Mufasa decimates him too, though
>You haven't done anything the whole game
>You barely used or swapped any cards because you couldn't encounter anything worth using them on
>You couldn't afford using any spell cards because you rolled some useless ones or too expensive ones
>You didn't hold any settlements for more than 2 turns because you've been restricted by mountain ranges, swamps and enemy AI
>You barely had any gold to buy yourself 2 items and take one more from a quest (the 2nd quest, the first one you failed)
>You've been torn apart on the inside by uncountable amount of inches from every side by Banes
>Your a$$ is as terrorized as your settlements
>You held on to 3 points of prestige
>Death of Mufasa granted you victory anyway
>You may have won, but the aftertaste of every Bane inch remains
That's basically what this game is. Random chance upon random chance upon random chance. Randomly generated maps with random spellcards and random dice rolls on every encounter. It feels like you have no control over anything in the game. And it's not anything like GoT either, there are no alliances, no betrayals, no bigger plans, just some random events you try to make the best of in unpredictable circumstances. No actual planned out strategy, political influence on the land or your allies, no nothing. You're at the mercy of RNGeezus to help you win the game, but you'll probably achieve that through random chance that the game lets you do it this time, rather than through your own cunning and skill.
Also, I've read a ton of complaints about annoying balance issues originating from DLC bought characters and such. As much as I didn't have the pleasure of experiencing this on my own, and as much as I disapprove of such policies in games in general, I can't say it anyhow affects my view on the game, because the game has too many problems within its basic playability for me to even care about anything beyond this broken foundation.

Valiant Hearts is a side project of Ubisoft and what a great side project.  While not particularly challenging, the game provides a few puzzles that will stump less experienced players for a while, and the player is well rewarded for making progress.  An interesting storyline showing the different and overlapping paths of the main characters, littered with interesting information about the Great War, which is both thought provoking and at times poignant, focussing on the human impact of the war rather than on the guns and glory on which so many other games tend to focus.  It won't take you long to finish the entire game, but it's well worth a look.

State of Decay at the time of release was an undersold and underhyped game that didnt get a huge amount of exposure which was a real shame. It combines a semi-open world environment ( your village, a neighbouring town, local theme park and the surrounding farm lands / roads) with a scripted story and randomly generated side quests as well as optional side story lines which affect the experience you will derrive from it.
Although the graphics are not the most amazing and the controls based on a port from consoles (or it feels that way as they are quite simple) the game itself is an absolute gem of gameplay, replayability, hidden RPG elements and immersive excursions in to the realms of zombie infested americana.
Even now I find it hard to think of a game which combines elements such as team morale, double negative decision making, resource gathering, zombie fighting, expansion planning and relationship managing in to one package where they seem to blend seemlessly together without any contrived mechanics.
Although zombie killing can become a tad repetitive the game adds in new zombie types, challenges and storyline events as you advance to constantly keep you thinking, adapting and stop you from getting complacent.
You want to expand your base with a watchtower for defence? Sure you can, but at the same time you need to gether resources to do it, will you have time to do that AND rescue the team member trapped on a food run? If you don't get the watchtower up will the zombie hoard fall on you and kill your base team? If you do both can you help your neighbours who have a missing person? What will the local factions think of your actions as you carry them out?
This is a game which is centered on GAMEPLAY in many ways, it will eat up your time as you realise you can befriend and use different charcaters in missions, as you realise you can ally / alientate different factions, as you realise you can make different decisions about key points in the game.

TY the Tasmanian Tiger. Where does one even begin with this beauty? My earliest gaming memories are of TY, exploring the Barrier Reef, and searching for lost koala children in the snowy mountian tops. I'll go more in depth about this little ripper.
TY the Tasmanian Tiger has a simple story:
You are TY, the last of the Thylacines (that's "Tasmanian Tigers", by the way).
Your family disappeared years ago, lost in a dimension known as "The Dreamtime", after the nefarious Boss Cass, a cassowary with dreams of world domination, sought to steal the five magical talismans which open a portal to said dimension. Luckily, they were spread across Austrailia after the Thylacines were lost, much to Cass' dismay.
But how do you learn about all this? Well, one day, when you were playing out in the forest with your Bilbie friends, you fell into a hole in the ground and met with a mystical Bunyip Elder. He told you the whole story, and so, with Murray the Cockatoo and Julius the Koala by your side, you set out to save your family.
The graphics in this game are truly something to behold, even for a game like this. The truly breathtaking, sandy plains of the Outback, the lush rainforests, the beautiful beaches. If you're looking for a game with beautiful, cartoonish levels, give this one a try for sure.
The gameplay is some of the best I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing. I'll lay this one out in sections.
The levels are so beautifully thought out, some wide open, with lots of area to cover, and even more places to search for collectables, and some narrow, but still very large, leaving multiple pathways for you to explore and many areas to visit and revisit, making for a great reason to backtrack and play the level again.
To protect yourself, you're armed with a pair of wooden boomerangs, which are only one pair of a large number of 'rangs that you'll be able to unlock throughout the course of the game, as well as your good old pearly white teeth. Bite and 'rang your way through those enemies!
The main section of gameplay is searching for collectables. These include:
Thunder Eggs:
By the end of this game, you'll have seen so many of these sparkling gemstones that you won't be able to think of anything else. They're the main collectable in the game, and are neccessary to access and defeat each area's boss level and acquire the magical talismans.
Golden Cogs:
These items will be necessary for the 100% completion, and to unlock new boomerangs to use in the many levels of this game. After you collect so many, a new boomerang is added to your arsenal.
Opals:
Opals are the rings, coins, wumpa fruit or gems of the TY universe, a whole 300 to collect per level. Don't you worry, though! They're not too hard to find, if you know where to look! Collecting all of them will... well, I'll let you figure it out.
The controls are pretty decent, when you use a Keyboard and Mouse, but I recommend using a controller. Either way, both styles can be fully customised, allowing you to find what controls work best for you.
TY can do basic functions like running, jumping and attacking, as well as being able to learn to swim and glide later on. The movement is quite smooth, and the jumping will almost never be a problem for you.
All of the aforementioned "Thunder Eggs" are acquired via a sort of mission system. In every level, there are a number of Thunder Eggs to collect, each obtainable through either completing a time attack mission, doing jobs for people, finishing minigames and collecting them whilst traversing each level, as well as saving your Bilbie friends (mentioned earlier, who raised TY after his family.
As great as the game is, there are some problems with it.
-It can be confusing at times, not knowing where to go now and then.
-One boss, namely
, can be pretty confusing if you don't know what to do. It's not made very clear at all.
-LENNY THE LYRE BIRD
-
are not very memorable or enjoyable levels, imo.
Overall, TY is a fun, charming little game that a lot of people can just pick up and play with little to no issue, and honestly, if you like character-based collectathons, you should definitely purchase this game.

Paint the Town Red is a game that is based on the practice of grabbing whatever you can pick up and smashing it into people's faces, torsos, arms, legs, etc.  It's a pretty simple concept, and the main draw to the game is, well, painting the town red. With blood. Is it fun? Yes, it is. Can it be improved upon? Yes, it can.
The gameplay is a simple melee-focused first-person fighter. It has many different types of weaponry, from chairs to nunchucks, from shotguns to katanas. The actual fighting in the game is very fun to pull off, being able to dismember your foes and brutally obliterate them. Not only do you get some insanely fun ways to take out your enemies with the objects in the environment, but you also get an array of 3 powers, one that pushes all enemies away from you, one that allows you to punch and kick people's limbs to bits, and one that allows you to point at someone and have lightning blow them up. The powers are fun, but they are incredibly difficult to obtain, often taking dozens of kills to unlock one powerup. I also found the delay from starting the powerup to actually getting to use them to be very long. I also found some of the slow motion effects to be problematic at times, but this can be disabled. The game also happens to have a massive problem with the framerate, often dipping very much. The textures also seemed to be very oddly placed in different locations, like eyes being on the top of the head, but this texture issue only happens on the head, not on the torso or limbs.
TL;DR, The main part of the game, the combat, is great. There are some technical issues and problematic texture placement, but the gameplay ultimately trumps these issues.

We have Fight The Dragon; an indie RPG from 3 Sprockets. Let’s get rocking.
The Good
FtD has an impressively high replay value. The game itself consists of thousands of 10 – 15 minute (on average) adventures for your character to go on. This keeps things interesting and ensures that you don’t get stuck in a quagmire of monotony.
FtD includes an editor which allows you to build your own adventures and maps and not only play them, but share them with the rest of the community. (Steam Workshop is a big plus to any game in my opinion.)
This game is rather addictive. You get into the “just one more” mentality and find yourself still slapping skeletons with bladed instruments hours later.
The graphics have their own charming quality to them and it is fun to see different maps on every adventure.
The Bad
Once or twice I’ve had my character glitch out and rocket across the screen which resulted in my death. Not cool.
The camera angle isn’t always the best thing for you.
The game is kind of dark no matter what your gamma is set to.
The Meh
As far as character customization goes, FtD has a limited amount to offer you. While there is Steam Workshop, there’s still not much too it.
Weapon and armor varieties are also limited and the same goes for enemy variety.
Verdict: Yea
If you’re looking for a solid time killer and/or something you can get together with your friends and play to have a great time, look no further. You can pick up Fight The Dragon here on Steam or you can watch the Humble Bundle End of Summer Sale and try your luck there. As always, thanks for reading.

Armello hits a difficult spot. A win in this game depends both on skill and luck, but favors skill. Very few board games have this ability. Even Magic: the Gathering doesn't feel this perfectly balanced. I have been able to win with every character I have played and never felt hindered in any way. The greatest element to this game is the multiple ways to win. And each has its own unique challenges. They also form a natural difficulty balance as some, such as soul stone or rot victories, are far more difficult than the simpler kill the king or presitige victories. In this way, you can choose how much difficulty you want without needing to alter the AI or find specific people to play against. The art is beautiful. The music is fantastic. There is nothing not to recommend here. Best board game on Steam.

Armello is a game that picks at your brain. You have to strategize, pay attention to your surroundings and it also puts you on edge with the challenges you're bound to face.
To be honest, at first this game didn't really peek my interest. Aside from the fact that the characters are animals (which I personally love), it never really spoke to me. Until a friend of mine encouraged me to give it a try. After that night, I was definitely hooked.
If you're not the type who has any patience, this game isn't for you. Being able to act first rarely happens (so far in my case, but it doesn't really bother me that much) and it would take a long wait especially when you're last. Because players WILL take their time in deciding what action to take. Definitely not for those who get irritated easily. It does get tedious to wait sometimes, but if you love these kinds of games it wouldn't be so much of a problem.
The graphics are very well made as well as the animation. I definitely love how the King's condition would change as the rot increases. I especially love how they named each and every tile differently, the devs definitely let their creativity flow. The only error I found so far was Mercurio's defense stance (when he gets attacked), the pupils in his eyes seem to disappear whenever this happens and I'm not sure if this is a connection problem, but if you get disconnected, the game gets stuck on an empty main menu screen, the only thing you can see is the backdrop. Other than that, everything seems to be working perfectly!
Keep up the good work, devs!

I really liked the look of Armello the moment I saw it, and was really happy when I got it in the July Monthly Humble Bundle. Unfortunately, it doesn't live up to its appearance.
PROS:
+ Excellent graphic style, really enjoyable.
+ Neat idea, creating a board game specifically for computer.
+ Acceptable music, atmospheric, but not too memorable.
CONS:
- Sooooo random. The mechanics are based on randomness, so you can get messed up by doing anything other than standing still. And even then... Battles are entirely based on dice, so more dice is helpful, but they make nothing certain. Exploring dungeons is random. And exploring dungeons can give you the Wanderer, which moves you in a random direction at the beginning of every turn. Perils are randomly placed and resolved by dice. Quests are randomly resolved. Terrain is randomly generated. In short, everything is random.
- Horrible victory conditions. There's Prestige victory (which requires military strength), there's Kingslayer victory (which requires military strength), there's Rot victory (which requires military strength), and there's Spiritseeker victory (which is totally random). So the only reliable victory path is military.
- Little-to-no RPG elements, besides choosing a character and bonuses.
- Lack of customization in exactly the areas where you would expect it. Most importantly, your deck. Most RPG games that involve decks give you some ability to customize the deck. Do they do that in Armello? Nope, of course not. They want randomness. So you pretty consistently draw cards that are poorly suited to your character.
- Tutorial is lousy, as is the pause screen.
CONCLUSION:
I'm very disappointed in this game. Find something else to play, this isn't worth your time.
FINAL RATING: 1/7

Purr-ty cute game. Get it? Because it's about cats?
Okay, you're not getting. The reason that this is funny is because CATS, the subject of this game, make PURRING sounds. Purr-ty is a combination of the words PURR and PRETTY. It's like I'm saying it's a PRETTY cute game, but I made a pun of it.
Disclaimer: I played this with a controller. The game functions with keyboard controls but seems better suited to a gamepad.
The game is short and sweet; should only take 2 to 3 hours to fully complete.
The hand drawn artstyle is purr-fect... Well maybe not perfect. There are a few spots in the game where it leads to a bit of visual confusion. Nothing game breaking, just a few obstacles that you might not know you need to jump over, ledges that aren't super obvious you can jump on them, and a few fish bone collectables that blend really well into the background.
The platforming mechanics are nice and tight. You can choose if you want your jump to be a single big jump or a double jump. I found the double jump to be more practical, though for all intents and purr-poses they're both the same.
Jumping up and down isn't the only thing you'll be doing though. Over the course of the game's 5 levels the platforming is mixed up with climbable plants, stealth sections, hazards like falling pots, dogs, and even old ladies.
Only other thing you should know about the game is that it is REALLY LOUD. In order to lower the game volume you need to load into a level and pause the game. Not a great place for the volume sliders, but meow you know.
Now before you get all bent out of shape because of my bad puns; remember that you're not Anthony Burch. You're life is pretty swell and you have no reason to be upset.

A run-of-the-mill collectathon platformer that's a bit like if you mixed a bunch of Sonic OCs with Mad Max Kidz. A very, very Australian game, to the point where if it wasn't actually made by Australians it would come off as grotesquely racist. The main character, Ty, speaks almost entirely in stereotypically Australian exclamations like some kind of tourism board mascot, which given that everyone else in the game speaks mostly-normally leads to him coming off as a touch surreal, like he was originally written as a silent protagonist who had dialogue hastily added into conversations held more at him than too him.
Story-wise, the game is as thin as it gets. I almost get the impression that the game was based on some sort of Saturday Morning Cartoon, the way the backstory is vaguely alluded to, characters come and go like we should know them already, and side characters go through cliche story arcs at breakneck pace. It's not that I didn't know what was going on - everything about the story was incredibly by-the-numbers - but it felt like somebody wrote a story twice as long and had it edited down.
Gameplay is basically passable, if annoying. You only gain two new moves throughout the game, aside from your ever-growing collection of boomerangs with increasingly redundant functions. The boomerangs themselves are fairly clumsy to use, despite being your primary weapon, as their range is extremely vague and their targetting is inconsistent, leading to many situations where you can throw one at an enemy five feet away and it'll whiz harmlessly past him and leave you unarmed for the next few seconds. However, the game's difficulty is almost nonexistent - the hardest achievement in the game is the one where you have to lose all your lives - largely due to Ty getting nearly 10 seconds of mercy invincibility every time he takes damage, meaning it honestly takes effort to lose a life to a single threat.
Ultimately, though, the game is honestly inoffensive. It was a functional timekiller, but I'm not going to give it a recommendation on the grounds that I wouldn't actually suggest anyone else go out of their way to play it. It's not bad, but it's hardly anything good either.

Here are just a few reasons to give this game a try:
Open World - Similar to the first two
titles,
utilizes a top-down open-world approach, which permits the exploration of the vast overworld on foot or with one of the game’s many unique vehicles. Within this sandbox are varying side missions, shops, secrets (featured later), a primary story arch, and non-player characters which stride throughout the area with their own agendas. Seeing as though the Player can wreak havoc in many different ways with both a large inventory of weapons and objects as well as utilizing vehicle collisions, police pursue the same principles as they would in early
titles: kill the Player. Apart from this perspective, the actual missions within the world are quite enjoyable; the primary quest-line advances the story and side quests typically give the Player access to unique equipment, vehicles, and services.
Free Roaming Mode - When the Player wishes to experience the sandbox action to
without having to focus on missions appearing on the mini-map and the loss of money as a death penalty, Free Roaming mode is always available from the Main Menu. Though some of the features are not accessible as they would be through the main game-such as completing various missions-, Free Roam spawns the Player with nearly every weapon available and practically pats you on the head while saying, “Go have fun!” There is absolutely not penalty for death-with a life tracker humorously tracing the Player’s deaths in the negatives-but the same overworld ‘police chase you if you do something bad’ theme still applies.
Humor -
features references mostly from 1980s popular culture such as
from the
and pop icon Michael Jackson, and presents these fairly bluntly throughout the territory. One instance would be a useable Warp Pipe-originally seen in the
franchise-which takes the Player to a run-down sewer system that presents themes from other titles such as
. Somewhat subtle remark placements, however, can be viewed in the game, though it does help to know or have heard of at least some icons from the 1980s to understand these.
Secrets - I prefer to allow Players to delve into this item on their own terms, but
retains its 1980s gaming feel by packing secrets all over the map, with both simple and complex means in which to attain and discover them. There is an array of enjoyable hidden content within this game, from unlockable Player skins to special objects. Keep an eye out! My word of advice: write down those codes; you will know what I mean.
TL:DR - Though simple,
is a highly enjoyable title that melds traditional themes with a ton of awesome gameplay mechanics. I do apologize for not writing much about this game in comparison to other titles, but I must admit that this one is one of my favorites regardless. I highly recommend giving this game a try; this is not a high-budget AA title, but its charm alone is what makes this game so engaging, with gameplay that entices the Player to continue the trek. For some reason, this game never got the credit it deserves. A GREAT game with LOTS of potential. Unfortunately, most of the bugs and problems may never be fixed, and a lot of its potential may never be redeemed. Google Sven Coop Sniper dev. Reddit is a good place for it to find out what all the fuss is all about.
Thing is - Sven coop devs, the once with the most power, are the once who can't be very productive. This is just a small project/hobby for them. They have full-time jobs and famillies and their own problems. They don't want to spend more time on it than they deem they can afford. Thus - their productivity rate is almost Valve-time. But that's not the bad part.
The bad part is - there were people who were really productive in the team. People that had the free time for the game. People who knew what they were doing. People who could fix problems that bugged the game for YEARS in just a few days, unlike the other devs who would just nitpick really minor problems and only work on them during full moons. People who could lay a better foundation for the game's future. Truly redeem its potential. Solokiller was one of them. And he had to quit. Why? Because his productivity was waaaaay to high for the rest of the dev team.
One of the team devs, the most powerful one, Sniper - insisted on checking everything, or doing it himself. And a lot of times, he would simply deny an action because - he either didn't have the time, or couldn't spend the effort, or didn't want others to fiddle with "his" project. He wanted to do this without ambition and without haste. He can't afford those because this is just a part time hobby for him. He complains about how he has a full-time job and he's doing it for free. Meanwhile, Solokiller was doing much more than he does in a MUCH shorter amount of time. The others just couldn't keep up with his pace and ambition, so he had to leave as he was not even given a chance (and access to the game's coding).
I think Sniper tries to make changes little by little to allow the game to be stable. But he refuses to tackle big problems, and instead relies on fixing smaller things. And it takes a LOT of time for them to fix even those things. Meanwhile, Solokiller fixed a lot of the biggest issues that plagued the game for years, but none of it was accepted to be even tested properly. A lot wasn't even viewed! I don't blame Solokiller for leaving. He's just "too good" compared to the rest of the team. They couldn't keep up, so they isolated him.
Sniper goes around such reviews, saying its irrelevant to the game reviews. But it IS VERY RELEVANT. The dev team makes the game. If the dev team is bad - the game will be bad. How is the game now? It works because the dev team exists. It is fine - but coming to this level took them a LOT of time, due to low productivity. They complain, and I get it - you are all grown up men with full time jobs and little time to spare. But if you can't do it right - find someone who can! Someone who has the time and the brains and ambitions to do it! And they did! And then they made it hell for him, forcing him to quit. How does that make sense?
Overall, I feel like they've just missed a one-time-chance here. See, GoldSrc is a VERY old engine, and Half-Life 1 (and Sven Coop) is a VERY old game. A lot of people nowadays haven't even touched Half Life 1, let alone know anything about using the GoldSrc engine and the coding of the game. Solokiller not only knows the engine and the game VERY well, but he also has the time, the effort and the ambition to fix and improve it. It is like finding a unicorn! And they just made it hell for him. Good luck finding someone else like him. You've just made probably one of your most productive members quit.
Do I recommend this game? Yes. While it took them AGES to get to this level - it is FINALLY on Steam and it is getting small updates every now and then. But what am I angry about? The potential they are wasting here. Sniper - if you're reading this - reconsider the way you operate and your structure. It is easy to say that you're doing this for free and in spare time - which is true. But why would you deny access and turn down the people who could do what you cannot (without atleast spending years on it)?

Casual solo/coop Star Wars platformer for children/parents+children. No more. No less. Most of the negative reviewers probably didn't expect this game (and its story) to be that obviously aimed for children and expected a little more, hence the negative reviews. Again, this is no Lego Star Wars which is "officially for children" but an adult can find fun in it too; this game doesn't aim for adults at all.
With that said, if you try to have an open mind about it and realize it's not really meant for you, as a game it's not that bad as you'd expect. It's obviously designed to be played with controller instead of keyboard/mouse, for which the controls (and camera) are pretty clumsy. The gameplay reminds me very much of some Playstation 1 platformers (kind of like Jedi Power Battles) and feels a little outdated (although the graphics are decent), but slashing stuff with lightsaber should be enjoyable enough for kids. Despite the level design not being the greatest (sometimes it's not clear what to do or where to go) it plays pretty well. The game is hardly challenging and even on hard difficulty you'll find yourself just swooping through the levels. But again, if you're reading this, this game is probably not meant for you.
I DO recommend it for parents/children (especially if they're Star-Wars-positive), it should be fun enough. Wait for some sale though, it's definitely not worth the full price. And get yourself a controller or two (it can be played either solo or by two players cooperating, which might be pretty fun), keyboard+mouse is playable but very clumsy. In contrary to some reviews, I had no problems at all getting it run on a modern system with Windows 8.1, just installed and played.
I DO NOT recommend it to more serious gamers who are looking for challenge, deep story or an adequate game, you'll be disappointed. Also, if you're a serious gamer, GFWL can be annoying to you.

I rated it:

I remember playing this game when I was very young. Some of my fondest memories were me trying to beat the Geonosis section for the first time, and dying over and over again because of those elite Geonotians picking me and my squadmates off one by one. Now, looking at this game through older eyes, and playing it all the way through, I can tell you that it is one of the best $10 I've ever spent.
In case you haven't heard of this game before, it takes place in the events of Attack of the Clones and Revenge of the Sith. You are part of Delta Squad, an elite group of four clones that are given tasks normally to covert or dangerous for normal clone troopers. You'll have to use your diverse arsenal, as well as team tactics to complete the tasks that are given to you.
PROS:
-Very nice visuals, that still hold up well after eleven years
-Solid voice acting all around, really fleshed out and loveable characters
-Excellent story, probably the best story of any of the prequel movies/games
-Combat is polished and exhilarating to play. Plenty of versatile tactical options
-Runs well on pretty much any competent PC; mine ran it at the highest settings at 60fps throughout
-Amazing soundtrack that combines John Williams' classic score with new and incredible music by Jesse Harlin
CONS:
-Some optimization issues for new hardware. In menus, the mouse sensitivity is waaaay too high to use, so you'll have to use arrow keys to navigate menus. Larger resolutions aren't present, so if you have a big screen, the game may look a little pixelated.
-I had one game-breaking bug. Delta 62 wouldn't move out of a corner, so I had to load my last save. That fixed the problem, but still annoying.
-Very abrupt ending in my opinion
-Game is kinda short (about 10 hours), but considering you're only paying $10 for it, I guess it's fine
-May be harder for new players. Even I, admittedly, had to swith the difficulty to Easy for a couple of nightmarishly hard sections
-No sequel. );
FINAL STATEMENT:
This game is by far the best singleplayer Star Wars game ever made. It's best quality is just how polished everything is, from it's grim and somber take on the Clone Wars, to the magnificent, tough-as-nails tactical combat. The beautiful soundtrack, the fantastic voice work, and the great graphics help suck you into the game even more. And by the end of it, you'll want more (even though EA and Disney will never give us any more). Sure, the passage of eleven years has given it a couple technical hiccups, but they pale in comparison to the rest of the game.
RATING: 9/10

Armello is a board game. A rather random one when i come to think of it, but enjoyable.
The story goes along something like this. There is this lion king who once rule the kingdom who fell ill because of corruption that has entered the kingdom. The king now rotten is spreading havock, and it is YOU who have to defeat him and overthrow the king so that peace can finally be ruled over Armello.
I think that's about right.
There are many ways to win at this game, you have to either kill the king without dying, or you can get prestigious, (gaining enought reputation to be called the new king), become even more rotten then the king, or collect enough crystal stones. There's probably one last thing I am forgetting... Oh well.
Without getting too much into the characters, there are 8 characters in the game available to you to choose from.(excluding the DLC characters of course.) Each with a unique skill/ability and stats for you to take advantage and exploit.
Once beginning a game, you and three other players will be put onto each corner of a map. The map is randomly generated, so take a good look of the map before doing something.
Depending on your amount of Wits your character has, you will be presented with a set of random cards. there are 3 group of cards.
-Equipement (Provides you weapons that you can use on others to inflict damage or to wear on your deck. You can have a maximum of three equipement on your deck at all time. Wish to replace a weapon? You will need to discard a card. (Unless for a specific character who can retain said item.)
-Magic (These cards will consume magic points which you can obtain from certain tiles on the map. they can range from healing you, give you a boost of speed/ action points, hurt someone or spawn one of those fancy crystals.)
-Trickery (These cards are the trap cards of the game. You can place them on tiles of the map in exchange of some cash, rot or prestige. You can also play them directly on players depending on the card,)
There are other group of cards of which you cannot choose/obtain for yourself. which are:
-Followers (They are obtained from quests (or dungeons) and will help you along your journey. You place them on your followers deck near your equipment deck.)
-King cards (These cards are cards that will determine how the day will playout. These cards are given to the player with the highest prestige. You can only choose one at the beginning of a day. You cannot keep the card to yourself.)
At the end of each rounds you will be pick a certain amount of cards depending on the amount of cards you've used during the previous round. The number of card you can hold will be determined by the amount of Wits your character has.
At the start of the game you will also be given the choice of three random quest. You can only pick one. These quest will provide you permanent stat boost for your character for the run/game you are currently playing and potentially cards that you can only find in quests upon completion. At the end of a quest, you will be given three other quests.
From there you start climbing your way to the throne. To help you along the way, you can capture settlements that will give you an income of cash. There will be dungeons and caves to explore with the potential of finding rewards, Forest that grants you stealth during night and mountain that will cost you 2 action points to go on, but will benefit you with a defensive advantage. There's also some stonehenge looking tiles which will heal you and can spawn crystal stones at the beginning of each nights.
Loyal guards will roam the map. Attack one and you will have a bounty on your head. Same thing if you try to enter the king's palace. If the guards are the one to attack you, you won't suffer any bounty.
Creatures called Bane will appear on the map at night at certain dungeons. they will terrorize villages and hurt anything on site. They are heavilly corrupted. Attack with caution.
Killing players/Bane or completing a quest will grant you Prestige. The one with the highest amount of prestige will be nominated the Leader and will be able to choose from two cards of the King that will change the way the two upcoming rounds will playout.
Attacking a guard, entering the king's palace or being victim of a player's certain card will lower your prestige. A king card may also lower your prestige if you don't meet a certain requirment in the card.
You may be victim of Rot. Rot will slowly kill you at each morning, You can heal yourself from corruption/Rot or you can embrasse the sickness and become more ill and therefore, gain an advantage. Gaining more rot will provide you more dice against pure/less ill entities. Although Stonehenges may hurt you.
Once completing a total of three quest, you will be given a key to the King's palace, which will grant you a path to fight the king without to worry about his security trying to prevent you from accessing the castle.
Now, the main concern some people might have with the game is... well it sounds too damn random, and it is. I don't mind the random cards and quests but it is true that not having a randomly generated map would make strategy less RNG based. Maybe the addition of a map to choose from would be great addition to the game and make it less brutal.
RNG problems put aside, the team at League of Geeks can be proud of the work they put into the characters. Each character don't feel superior to an other. Which is something considering there are 8 characters in this game to choose from. +another 8 characters if you include the DLCs which are also very interresting. It all comes down to how you like to play Armello.
But don't expect a ultra silky smooth experience while playing the game. On my end i'v encountered a few glitches and bugs here and there but nothing major nor game breaking, but i'v heard some people complaining about some bugs appearing over the new updates that made their experience a little bit less enjoyable. so keep that imind.
Overall, the game is a blast with friends. I find to enjoy the game even with strangers or computers. I love the simple, yet somewhat complex system the game has. But PLEASE! for the love of god do consider doing your OWN research before buying this game. i may have oversimplified some things about the game. so better be safe then sorry.

This game is an example of basically everything you shouldn't do in game design.  Key points:
1)  It's a "why is there a board?" game.  There is no strategy in this game, period.  Everything is completely random.  You have to play the style your random cards force you to play.  You have to go where the random tile events take you.  You have to make friend and foes based on the random cards they have.  To say this is a game of skill is like saying a coin toss is a game of skill where you have completely freedom over the outcome because you get to pick heads or tails.  So why even have a board?  It's nothing more then the flashing lights on a slot mechine.
2) The only way to deal with the "random" is your characters traits ... they are the only reliable thing in the game and the only way to get even a basic amount of control back from the dice.  And because of this, this game is pay to win on a level that would make Farmville cry with shame.  The paid characters are better in every way.  Period.
3)  Game tries very, very hard to not be fun.  You know what's awesome about playing a game for 45 minutes where you make any decision perfectly and where everything goes your way, for 45 only to lose everything because someone who did nothing all game manages to roll 17 attacks with 2 dice while your role 0 with your 15 dice?  Nothing.  Not one thing.  This is a COMMON event, and even in single player you can't save and reload.
It’s one of the games you play a few times and think “wow, this game is wonderful in it’s style, art and ideas, it would have been FANTASTIC if it was made by a team that has even a passing acquaintance with what makes a game enjoyable”.
Sadly, it wasn’t.

When you boil it down, Epic Snails is a simple tank shooter, but what sets it apart is the fun artstyle and its accessibility to any age. While most tank games would have you trekking through large gritty battlefields, Epic Snails brings you back to your childhood days of playing in the back yard with either your friends or some toys. Most of all this game brought me back to the early days of Club Penguin, chatting with my friends and playing fun minigames. Which comes to no surprise since... well, Rocketsnail made this game afterall!
The main gimmick of the game is that, much like a snail, you can climb literally any surface you want. This introduces some unique senarios where, unlike traditional tank games, you or the opposing team can have a significant height advantage.
There are currently only a few weapons to choose from, and it seems like the basic cannon is the best of them by a large margin. That doesn't mean the other two aren't fun to use, you should simply pick the one that fits your playstyle.
The game is in very much in its early stages, and there's a lot to be improved. The controls can be finicky at times and the camera can do all sorts of crazy stuff. At the time of this review there's currently only one map (with a winter one on the way) and a small selection of hats. Overall I feel Epic Snails has a lot of potential. In the future we'll see new weapons, maps, and customizables for our snails that will further bring the game to life.
If you were/are a fan of Club Penguin, I highly reccomend giving this game a go, and be sure to give the team feedback so this game can reach is fullest potential!

The Purring Quest is a 2-4 hour experience in which you jump your way through a handful of levels. Your main objective is to reach the end of a level. There is also a collection mechanic by which you are rewarded for exploring and collecting 200 fish bones, a secret item, and recuing a kitteh that has been caged up!
The narrative is pretty straightforward. You are a cat looking for your owner who has walked off. (how rude!)
Gameplay-wise, I felt the platforming was decent enough. I do want to note that there is a split millisecond delay between pressing jump and your cat jumping. It wasn't annoying enough to be distracting, as you get used to it relatively quick as you jump your way through each level. You definitely have a weight that keeps you from making super ridiculous leaps. That being said, at the beginning of the game you can choose to have on or the other; a couble jump, or a super high jump. Depending on how you like to platform, either seems to be adequate enough to locate all the items in each level. I personally preferred double jump so that I could fine tune some more difficult jumps as I needed.
The music is also worth listening to. Very chill and soothing piano music!
Definitely worth a play if you enjoy platformers and cats! There aren't enough games on Steam where you play a cat, so this was a nice play through.
