There is an indescribable charm about this game that I just can't get over. I picked it up during the Summer Sale because it was less than three bucks. My expectations going in were for an hour-or-two-throwaway, barely finished product.
What I got instead has enthralled me so much the past two days. I can play for five minutes or get lost in a two-hour binge. The maps are long enough to feel detailed but short enough to complete in one sitting. Combat can get repetitive but with new and better loot dropping here and there, from enemies and chests, I didn't really care; it's good, plain fun. There are four classes with individual spells and special abilities - a fighter, fire mage, ice mage and rogue - but I've only played as an "Ice Wizard" up to this point without losing any interest or even gaining a desire to try other classes. I'm having too much fun with this one.
There's also a map/adventure/campaign editor where you can create your own landscapes, buildings, villages, etc. etc. You can also script NPCs to talk to the player when he approaches as well as decorate your worlds with trees, rocks, fountains, bookshelves, beds, chairs... You name it. With a touch of detail here and there, worlds come alive. The editor has some rudimentary logic chains and pressure pads so that you can create some quite interesting and complex puzzles, though I'll admit, I haven't delved into that area quite yet.
Buy this game. You will not regret it. I haven't had this much fun playing a game in who knows how long.

In Armello, the current Lion King is Infected with Rot and is dying. It is up to you to save the day by killing the current king and taking his place, waiting for him to die and taking his place or save him by purifying him of his Rot. Choose a hero from one of the 5 races and pit your random skills against 3 other players.
The gameplay is fairly straightforward with each player taking 3 actions on their turn. There are 3 different cards to draw from, Items, Spells and Trickery. There are 2 other types called Treasures and Followers. Each card requires a different type of resource to play. Items and Trickery require Gold while Spells require Magic. Item cards also require 1 of your 3 inventory slots. Some cards may even require a special type of resource called Rot. Confusing?
Conclusion, it isn't as fun as it is advertised due to the pseudo random number generator. You might as well have decided who wins by rolling dice at the start of the game. The skin shop is another money grubbing scheme that irked me. You have a buy to play game so it's not free to play. Why are so selling more DLC? However, the artwork and animation is pretty decent and I think that this is its saving grace.
Note: Armello is done by League of Geeks cofounded by Trent, Blake and Ty.
1. Guaranteed End
Maximum of 18 turns due to the King having 9 health.
2. Beautiful Visuals
The art of Armello is wonderful. The different artist names are revealed for certain cards. Yet, the style is somewhat consistent.
3. The 5 Races
Pretty interesting. You have Bears, Wolves, Rats, Rabbits or Bandit. It's a pity that there has been no new release of any race after the Bandits.
1. Zooming Out to Clouds
Why do I zoom out to clouds? I want to zoom out to a strategic view so I know where all the other heroes are at a glance.
2. Pseudo Random Number Generator (RNG)
I am not here to play a game based on feelings. I don't want to play Armello the game that makes you feel this way and that way. It sucks. I want to have planning, not dice rolls deciding the victor.
3. Small Map
It's small at 4 hex rings. You just don't get the feel that it's an epic quest. Rather, it feels more like a claustrophobic cluster ♥♥♥♥. It doesn't help that there is no reliable method to reach the opponent on the opposite side of the grid. Since the castle is in the way, it takes far longer to go around.
4. Dice Design
There are 6 faces on the Armello dice.
a. Miss
b. Explode (Score and roll again)
c. Defence
d. Attack
e. Sun (Only counts as hits during the day)
f. Moon (Only counts as hits during the night)
By default, you are meant to fail 33% of the time. If you want a specific face like defence, you only get it 16% of the time. This wasted dice is akin to doing nothing in the game. There is no strategic play just an empty dice that you might as well have not rolled. The variance is very large. You could roll all misses compared to all infinite explosions.
5. Random Everything
Combat - RANDOM
Dungeon Explore - RANDOM
Perils - RANDOM
Followers - RANDOM
Quests - RANDOM
Card Draw - RANDOM
Political Decisions - RANDOM
Stranger Follower - RANDOM
What choice do you have?
6. Dungeon Explore
You wonder what you explore the dungeon for? The rewards can only possibly be +4 Gold, +2 Magic, random teleportation to another dungeon, summon a Bane or get a follower.

State of Decay is what you would call " Sand Box Zombie Survival game with a bit of Micro Management". By far it is not a best game if you are looking for a story to gripping on. Buttttt if you are looking for an experience of "manage to survive in zombie apocalypse" this is a game for you.
The game can be very much sum up into this.
- You got yourself a base. Where there are main resources such as Ammo, Food, Medicine and Construction Material as a heart of your survival. Ammo will determine the auto resolve when horde of zombies raiding your homebase when you weren't around. Food....well, Is food. The more food you have the better morale your little group will be. Medicines are the same as Food and lastly. Counstruction Material, Where you can use for constructed a stations or barricade your base.
- The resources mentioned above will decrease as time went by. So you'll have to scavange for more resource. By explore the building around the vicinity. The resource in this building will be deplete as you finishing looted them. Which will force you to either go for "High Risk High Gain" by increase the radius of scavenging or you could relocate your homebase.
- Zombie usually came in group and will react very fiercely to any noise. Car engine, Running, Gun Blasting or even sound of melee combat. But also there are a Special kind of zombie such as Juggernaut, Feral, Bloater and Armor zombie, Each are required a different approach to dealth with.
In Overall this game can hook you up quite very long in term of sandbox and getting by with your little group of survivor....... That alone should be enough  to give this game a "recommended up". But if you, Like me, are looking for a "story experience" I would really like you to continue reading on a bit.
At first start, The game may seem to lean heavy on story. But after a few couple of "errand run". The game will start to open up for you to play in very much of ..... well. "Get to that check point, doing this doing that and return to base" and that's it. This may seem to be a good idea on first few hour. But after a long while, You'll start to experience the boredom which is not suppose to happen in a game about zombie surviving.
There are some "event" that seem to be very much a gameplay potential (Infected Survivor, Shifty Characters etc.) but as the game went on, These events seem to exist only just that. There are no story to grip on much here aside the one you will encounter from sandbox experience. Which can be very much vary from person to person. I could care less for any characters in this game at all. All death are just MEH and nothing more.
So if you are looking for a grand heart breaking zombie survival experience alone. You might want to skip this game. That's all I wish to say about this game.

So I just wanted to put my specs out there before I write this review just to say "I meet more than the reccomended"
So currently I am on 13.2 hours of this game (10.2 in the past week) and it is obvious the game does not want me to comeplete it as it wont stop dropping frames and crashing.
Here is my review:
The game starts off somewhat promising with the story of two brothers in the army in the middle of a mission when something bad happens to your brother and you end up on a mission in Georgia (The Russian Version) and you think your brother
is somehow involved. So thats Cliche 1 and 2 covered (Set in Russia, My
is involved).
With all other issues (Abridged) over compressed cutscenes, predictable story with twist, janky mechanics, no replayability, feels like an Ubisoft game (FarCry - Play Farcry with a sniper, Assult Rifle and Pistol (You probibly already do)).
As an Avid fan of FarCry this game feel very similar but feels like FarCry 2 - Not interesting, boring, very repetitive, many issues (See below)
(1) Veriety of Guns
(2) Repetitiveness and Difficulty
(3) Animations and Textures
(4) World and Map
(5) Conclusion
--------
(1)
That is all I will say about the story apart from Cliche 3 - The plot twist - which you see coming about the end of Act 1.
Now in terms of Gun Customisation there is a fair amount to go on, You can run a 7.62mm Rifle, 3.38mm Rifle or a .50 Cal rifle each with theirs own pros and cons (Sliencer & bipod availability) as well as a decent amount of secondary rifles/ shotguns/ bows as well as a small selection of Pistols (9mm or .45apc).
--------
(2)
Now lets talk about the 2 difficulties you can start with - No matter how hard you play the game, Just do the following
1) Don't get seen
2) Always use a Suppressor (as there is no reason not to)
3) Hold Right Mouse Button
4) Zoom in (depends on distance of target)
5) Hold Shift
6) Line the guys head up with the little diamond
7) Fire
Thats it really - the only difference is how hard the bullets hit. (Game has no cloud save and I had to reformat - played 2 hours on hard and learnt this)
-------
(3)
The Animations - these are the jankiest things I have ever seen.
Everything is so heavy - there is no need for that.
The Models - Ugliest things you will ever see in cutscenes
I swear to you now the game looks better when playing than it does in the cutscnes. Textures look dirty and muddy, blury and low res like they were compressed something awful. They are so few that an extra 10GB for some good cutscenes on 1080p should not be an issues (I think there is like 5 in total)
The speed you move at just does not fit - a car doing 80KM/ph is going at about 60mph. Honestly does not feel like it though. Imagine being on a rollercoaster and your vision does not blur around the corners as you gain speed going downwards. Running as well, I have never seen someone sprint so slow and cover as little ground as the main protagonist does.
-------
(4)
This is the most empty game world ever. There is a "fun" side mission for money called "Most Wanted" - you essentially kill 16 High Value Targets found in compounds (no achievement for clearing these compounds as far as i am aware and theres a fair amount of them in all sections). Now if you are in the area and get bored by all means go for the target - they are only worth 2500TP (TP is currency) to put this into sheer facts - Thats not enough for a decent rifle, nowhere close. I use the Knight 110 - Semi Auto, No bipod attachments, 24x variable scope, large mag. Cost 10,000+TP. The only reason to go for these "High Value" targets is for the achievements (25%, 50%, 70% and 100% in 1 playthrough). To put this into better terms - You get more fir raiding a wallet you find in a house marked with a diamond.
Now the map (or Maps as I believe there are 3) they are filled with little "(?)" just plotted and these are literally everything - Fast Travel unlocks, collectibles, "Extreme navigation Challenges" (neither extreme or challenging just push CTRL), Collectibles in compounds etc. Every played an Ubisoft game? Essentially that - an empty map full of trivial♥♥♥♥♥♥to do to keep completionists happy. The majority of the map is just filler.
-------
(5)
Ever played an Ubisoft game? Yeah its essentially that - This is not a typo or me forgetting what i was saying.
That is the best way to describe it. I simply cannot reccomend this game to anyone unless you are already a fan of the series. This game basically tries to cast as wide a net as possible to catch as much as possible.

So i finally pulled the trigger on what my instincts said was probably a good game despite its rating.
And of course I am always right and cannot possibly be wrong. That being said, lets talk about some honest points in the game. So damn many of the bad reviews are just "Its bad, trust me, dont get it" Well, sorry mystery moron, but we dont trust you.
Alot of people are comparing this game to a farcry style game. I think thats a bit misleading, this game felt much more like an early metal gear solid game in first person. Hear me out on this. A common trope of many base raid games out there today, from farcry to the phantom pain, is a total lack of interior bases. Ghost recon wildlands too suffers from this. What I mean with that is that most of these games give you no reason not to just snipe the base for a dozen minutes then be done. Theres no place where you can justify "Going in" and playing like a navy seal or SAS operative. Doing so in those games is essentially irresponsible because all the outposts are open air and honestly BORING.
This game, despite being advertised as a sniper game (Its sniping IS good) has a large amount of bases that have exterior components, but in addition to those have great interior areas. Areas where you are forced to sneak around with your handgun and silencer trying not to get blasted. I love that, I MISS that in newer games. Even the metal gear series, which is THE name in infiltrating close quarters combat games, has become a game where theres almost no interior spaces to infiltrate.
So in addition to that, this game does the "Approach the base from any angle" mechanic better than almost any other game ive ever played. Again comparing to metal gear TPP and farcry, most games that advertise multiple entries to bases have a few extremely obvious ways into the base or just sticks their bases out in the middle of deserts where you can literally come at it from any side because theres nothing stopping you. Sniper: Ghost warrior on the other hand, has so damn many ways into each base that in the course of doing a mission, you may spot 5-6 other ways you could have come into the base. Theres HUNDREDS of cliffs and mountains and bases to climb all over (Yes, full climbing system) and most of these bases also have at least 2 or so "Sneaky" entrances such as sewers to use as well. In TPP, you see miles of cliffs and you can climb up one tiiiiiny little crack in one rock that doesnt really boost your ability. In this game, if you dont spend part of every mission climbing, you are doing something wrong.
The sniping in this game is pretty complex by most gamers standards, but is taught well and can be watered down or made more realistic with difficulty settings. I liked it, though many may find it to be difficult if they aren't big buffs on wind and bullet drop. Play on easy mode if you are simply not good at this kind of sniping, you get a marker that shows you where the round hits.
Now that ive bragged on the part of the game some, let me give you some cons and other info that you should consider
Lets get it out of the way right off the bat. The story is awful. They should have just shipped the game with a realistic navy seal SOCOM style storyline but they instead made it dramatic with fantasy elements and that just drags down the experience. Would have been better to have had no story at all than what we got. Best to just ignore it and play the game like theres no crappy story, you will be better off.
As far as extra info goes, the game has a good spread of weapons and gadgets, but many of they are unlocked late game. This is an issue because you CANNOT replay missions. Yep, more on that below..
WHAT WERE THEY THINKING?! This game is so much fun with so many opportunities to sneak around and try out different strategies, and NO REPLAYING OPS? WHAAA? God that is infuriating, it should be a given that an open world game has replayable missions but NOPE! Unless you love replaying games like this WITHOUT new game + Then you will likely only get one playthrough and whatever fun you had after roaming around clearing outposts and targets.
the game has 4 acts with about 5 side missions and 5 main missions each, give or take. Side and main missions give you toys, but so does searching around and exploring. This is a bummer because its entirely possible that by the time you finally have the guns you want, you may have already beat the game and have nothing left to do with them.
Im gonna sneak in a comment about the RPG part of this game. The game features 3 really basic skill trees with skills that are pretty generic and common to games, HOWEVER, the system of awarding points is actually one of the best ive ever seen in a game. It can tell based on little actions what kind of player you are. For instance, it can literally tell if you are a warrior by the fact you fought through a rooftop ambush, OR if you are a "Ghost" which is given to you if you jump off the roof into the water. It literally awards you points with a title "escaped via rooftop jump". It even tracks if you sneak by enemies or take certain paths and factors that in. Would be much more enjoyable if these points did more than unlock basic perks but the fact that it reads who you are based on how you play is impressive and kind of compliments you for doing things your way rather than yelling at you for trying to do things your own way like most games do. the stealth is also less "Unfair" to you to most games. If a bad guy sees you, even gets a shot off at you, if you subdue him before he can call it in, the rest of the enemies will not know you are there.
So time for a conclusion, what do we have? A game that was terribly released without its planned multiplayer component (Coop or a mission designer would have suited this game so damn good..) and doesnt even have mission replayability to let you enjoy the thousands of ways you can go about doing your missions. Its easy to see how this missed potential led to the mixed reviews it has now.
However, as far as gameplay goes, this comes as close to the "Good old days" of metal gear and socom as ive gotten in a long time. You really can take on the persona of a spetnaz, SAS, or navy seal operative if you lose yourself in this game. Great stealth, great sniping, fun and intense combat (That on hard or super difficult mode is actually a huge challenge) Make for a game that excels in the gameplay department and fails pretty badly in the story and extra features departments. The sad thing is that if they shipped this with no voice actors, no story, and just a sort of "Mission select" screen with text describing the missions, it may have had a much better rating. If they just added mission replayability or at the very least an outpost and target reset button, this game would be improved by 100%.
Final verdict: I got it on sale for 22.49 and feel like I got my moneys worth. I satisfied my navy seals craving and will likely come back to this game to explore the world and take outposts until I have nothing left to do. at 10 hours in Im on the last act and have done 0 exploring or outposts or extra targets, just side missions and main missions, so the game is not lacking in length.
If the devs wanna make something groundbreaking, they should take this games engine and system and make a game that calls back to SOCOM 1 and 2, coop and everything, throw in the easy to use level editor from farcry 4 and it will be worth gold.
Final Thought
If I had to sum it up in one statement, I was impressed at how well this game lets any gamer play stealth (Or loud, when its not mission critical) to their style. I never had a moment where a strategy I wanted to try wasnt plausible. With luring rocks, spotting bullets, luring bullets, shotguns with slugs or buckshot, heavy machine gun with a silencer, and a slew of gadgets from gas mines to throwing knives, you really can play the stealth type you love.

A great game for fans of simple, FPS shooters, but it is also a relatively hollow game, all things considered.
-The gameplay is fun, and the ability to command your squad is a unique gameplay mechanic.
-There are no upgrades, collectibles, or unlockables, and the levels are fairly linear. This can be good, bad, or a little of both, depending on your personal preference.
-The story is minimal, but definitely there. The characters are likeable, but relatively static, and the narrative is pretty surface level. The ending is very sudden, and doesn't really give the player much resolution.
-The game is very stable, with very few bugs, but the few bugs that can occur were, at least in my experience, very noticeable, though not game-breaking.
-The game can be very nostalgic for fans of shooters from the mid 2000s (arguably the peak of shooter games), and the story may be quite interesting for Star Wars fans (I believe this game is still canon, in case you were wondering).
-There is virtually no replayability, but considering the current price for this game, the 9-12 hours of gameply you'll get are well worth what you'll pay.
-The graphics aren't bad at all, especially for its time.
Overall review = 6/10

Fallout Tactics is not, as many seems to think, the third fallout game. It is a spin-off, set in the time between the two original Fallouts and focusing almost entirely on the one aspect of it's predecessors that was almost universally disliked, squad combat.
As you head off into the wasteland one more time you will find some comfort in the familiar. The SPECIAL system is still in place and allows you to customize both yourself and the squad with which you are now required to do battle beside. Memories of NPC burstfiring and having Marcus in your team at all can quickly be dismissed however as your entire squad is completely under your control this time.
Battles play out in either the regular turn based mode which with a big team, big maps and lots of enemies make the game dreadfully slow at times, or a pseudo-realtime mode that lets everyone act out their turns in concert with each other. The real time mode might make some of the smaller battles fly past quicker but as it was obviously never part of the core mechanics it comes with a whole slew of problems that makes it unusable when faced with bigger enemy parties, most notably each character will only perform one action at a time and will then stand around afterwards, waiting to be told to fire off his gun for a second time.
The great writing of the old Fallout's make a return, although in a more condensed format and lots of the over the top humor from Fallout 2 is present as well making the non-combat segments of the game quite enjoyable, the non-linearity and the choice and consequence system from those games are not present however.
Graphically the game feels dated, a long time has passed since the original Fallout and not much has changed since then. The soundtrack still contains some gems and the game does succeed in places at re-creating that Fallout fell. Those instances are unfortunately quite rare.
All in all Fallout Tactics is a game that takes too much away from what is tried and true. It tries to create a new experience in a medium with which it has little familiarity and the many rookie mistakes shines through all too much. This makes this a hard game to recommend, even for a die-hard Fallout fan such as myself.

This game is quite a lot of fun!  It does indeed feel like a mashup of Diablo and Little Big Planet.
The shining star for me is the ACK, the tools that let you create adventures. While there are plenty of tool here to make a fullout adventure and even campaign, the basics of the tools allow one to create, more or less, a dungeon.
I'm impressed, certainly, by the ease-of-use of the tools.  I'm sure I'm not the only one among us, but very rarely do I read tutorials or hints and tips before using a toolset such as a level editor.  For me, I generally only retreat to tutorials if I can't figure out how to do something that I'm trying to do.  All that to say, I've not needed to look at pretty much any documentation to use these tools, they are that simple to use.  (I am a programmer by trade, though.)
I sort of wish that there were some sort of an option to intentionally "complicate" the editor in order to get a little more mileage in terms of efficiency and final product quality, but I completely understand some of the design decisions that were made.
As far as gameplay goes, it's solid.  It's nothing groundbreaking, but it's nothing to complain about.  If you like ARPGs, then you'll probably like this one.  The only things I've taken note of are the predictable and exploitable AI and a probable class imbalance (There are four classes).
The loot shrine is a genius idea.  for those that don't have the game, the loot shrine is basically a place where you can "sell" items and donate gold.  The more accrued value you accumulate, the better the item and rewards you get when you finally cash-in.  It gives you a mostly random output, with the player having a small amount of choice in what their reward is.
Another unique aspect of this game is the dragon.  He's a really tough enemy which, I'm assuming, drops some of the best loot.  You get loot at certain milestones of health you take away from the dragon.  You can only fight the dragon, though, if you have enough tokens (Dragon Scrolls).  Each Dragon Scroll gives you a certain number of attempts to
.
I've not dabbled too much in fighting the dragon because I'm still fairly new and he stomps me...
As a plus, the developers and community seem quite helpful (see comments in this review) and responsive.  There were a few bugs (and a mistake on my part) that have both recently been addressed and corrected with goodwill and no malice, despite my (then) stated disappointment.  That being said, there are likely more bugs, but as of now I don't know of any that I've come across that haven't been fixed.  You'll likely not find anything gamebreaking, just things that might irk you.
I sincerely hope the developers will work on a sequel and are able to take what they learned from this game to make a spectacular new game, although not in any sort of a hurry as this game still certainly has mileage left.  Sort of like LBP, which is a sited inspiration on the store page.  The first LBP was great, but had some kinks.  LBP2 seemed to work most of the little kinks and bugs out and was an excellent builder in nearly every right.
TL;DR  Great adventure editor, easy to use.  Pretty good gameplay.  Possible occasional bugs.

Bandits DLC characters are "high risk-high reward" and introduce a couple new mechanics in the way it's played.
Usurpers DLC characters so far, are slightly OP. With innate skills that others could only obtain via cards if they are lucky.
There are 4 ways to win every game. And depending on the type of victory you are pursuing, you may want to benefit or sabotage other players.
Eventually you'll find yourself in a match with 3 turns left, with each player trying to achieve victory a different way, after all 4 palace walls are down, no obstacles, the king about to die. Everybody trying to kill each other. Good times.
One of the best ways to kill time.

Let's just start off and say that it is a cute little game with what I'd consider a rather pleasant art style, in fact the small spurts of kitty jokes and "
" moments combined with how the game has been drawn up is what pretty much made the game for me personally. After playing through all the levels and finding all the collectibles I ended up falling short of just
so if you're looking for an extensive game this is certainly not for you, it's more like a quick fuzzy experience that will warm you up, probably a great game if you're feeling down and need to get your mind off things.
Gameplay wise it's alright and nothing over the top. Controlling your character doesn't have too much feel to it and I'd class it more more like a well made flash game on that aspect which can be taken as you wish. The platforming is not by any means challenging when it does come up, so it just strengthen the idea of the game being a relaxing experience with kitties rather than a challenging puzzle and platforming game. The game allows you to play both with a keyboard and an xbox controller so that's a plus! And the controls feel solid enough so any seasoned player should not have too many problems or frustration going through the story and enjoying the game as a whole.
What I personally would've liked would be a longer game, where maybe the different areas of the game would have more than one level to give some more sense of travel since the game sure is, very short. Maybe some interesting cutscenes inbetween the levels instead of a "Straight into action from the menu" sort of take, since it feels like the game would benefit from this and give players something more to get invested in. The game also lacks much replayability once you've ran through it which is also a bummer. As far as the challenges and platforming goes I would've liked it getting even more tricky down the end of the game, but since there's not much room to expand a difficulty curve it makes enough sense that it was made the way it was.
Over all I think despite the shorter play time and the price tag I found this a welcoming game and I enjoyed myself. Snatch this game up on a steam sale and there should not be any regrets, just don't come in with high expectations as this game was probably a feat by itself on limited resources.

The Purring Quest:
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Cats are well-known for their extreme urge for adventure; most of them are waiting for you to open a window or door to escape the lovely home you provide them. Then they come back when they need food or curling around you. Well this time around, the cat wants to find his owner, and boy oh boy, now I know why cats have seven lives to spare - they really need them! Jump into the Purring quest and find out why?
The Purring Quest is a 2D platformer where you take control of Kimchi, a cat who is on a quest to find his owner. As you launch the game, you will see what’s about about to happen to Kimchi, and why it wants to find his owner. It is a rather emotional start to the game (without spoiling it). The quest itself has five beautiful levels and you will have to collect fishbones (200 per level), a hidden cat and a collectable. Scratching posts will be laid out at intervals within each level.  As you pass each of these posts, your progress is automatically saved. You will lose one of your seven lives if a dog catches you, especially the nasty chihuahua and/or the adorable doberman. Other animals, like the pigeon, are to be avoided, or you can hit them with your little paw to get rid of them, but make sure your timing is right, otherwise you will lose another life! You might be aware that cats will always land on their feet no matter what - but what happens if the length of the fall is very high? Well, you will lose another life. Pots will drop from windows and even pigeon droppings can be a challenge to get through! Kimchi will meet other cats (famous cats, I may add) during his journey, with whom he will have a little conversation, or even be offered something to help him on his quest.
I really like the graphics and animations in this game; really well executed and the game runs smoothly. You can use either the gamepad or the keyboard for the controls but I personally prefer using the gamepad. Good, smooth soundtrack, too.
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Good graphics
-	Good Story
-	Good Soundtrack
-	Fun and challenging at times
-	Achievements and trading cards
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	No difficulty option
I really enjoy The Purring Quest, a 2D platformer with a good story. Definitely a game to own!

The Purring Quest is a cute platformer where you play as a cat. The game takes place on a twodimensional plane where you (the cat) has to jump, climb, claw weaker enemies, and avoid bigger enemies like dogs.
Along the way there are collectibles: each level has 200 rotten fish to find, one trapped cat, and one other item.
The strengths of the game are in how it feels like you really are playing a cat, with a world that looks to scale and plausible dangers. It is an 'epic quest' but on cat scale.
There is no voiced dialog, but at several times the story is told through textboxes. Which is a bit of a shame as the game intro is completely textless but succeeds perfectly in telling the game's story, and is excellently animated for this game style.
Good points are how good the main character is controllable -- as long as you use a controller. The game offers two different jump styles: long jump and double-jump. You can switch as you start the game to a style that you like best.
I also tried keyboard controls, but they don't feel as responsive as the  controller does.
The levels are all relatively easy to get through with a boss fight or other challenge at the end, but they're all very possible. The challenge comes from finding all hidden items.
In level three you get a hiding ability that made me laugh... Solid Cat.
Bad points are that the game occasionally likes to hide enemies behind foreground effects. This leads to a cheap death. You do get seven lives and even if you die seven times you can respawn at a checkpoint, but cheap deaths are never fun. You also have falling damage... for a cat. Thematically that just feels wrong.
The game starts in a pretty dark level at a graveyard which may be too scary for younger players - not that anything bad happens, but the mood can be scary. Afterwards everything is lighter and more fun so if playing with a young child consider starting them at level two.
Overall fun game and definitely worth checking out if you like platformers.

You know how some people say that cats just don't really care about humans- that the only reason they put up with us is because we scratch their fur, feed them whenever they ask, brush them and scoop the cat box? Well... this game kind of disproves all that, all the while offering some fairly decent platforming action. There's even a sweet little story to go along with it- and to top it off, the game is challenging, but not overly so. You won't throw your controller down in frustration, not even once. This time around, wash your fur and straighten out those whiskers, we're reviewing The Purring Quest.
This game has you taking on the role of Kimchi, a cat that is owned by an older gentleman. The opening montage to the game tells of a bittersweet story-a young man falls in love and marries his dearest, and then they adopt a cat- Kimchi. They live for many years in peace and happiness, until one day... the wife falls ill and passes away from some unexplained illness. This leaves Kimchi's owner in a state of shock, and he ends up just living with his cat for many more years- developing what appears to be some form of Alzheimer's as depicted by the pictures on the wall flickering and fading away. However, Kimchi is essential to reminding him of the current day- and all is seemingly good. Until... he takes Kimchi out to visit his wife's grave at the cemetary, and ties his leash up to a fence post to make sure he doesn't run off while he visits the grave. He spots a woman that looks amazingly like his departed wife did when she was young, and he ends up wandering off after her, dropping a picture necklace that might be the only thing that can jog his memory. Kimchi panics- his owner has just left him all alone in the graveyard, and to make matters worse, some crow just swooped on down and stole his owner's locket. Struggling out of the harness, Kimchi starts to make his way back to the city to locate his lost owner.
The game consists of five levels- the graveyard, the village, the gothic quarter, the city, and the skyscrapers. You'll need to complete each one in order to finish the game. There aren't any secret levels as far as I know, but what there are in each level are things to collect and famous cats to meet. There's no sign of Grumpy, but you'll end up meeting cats like Nora the piano cat, Oskar the blind cat, Nala, Cooper the photographer cat, and Henri "Le Chat Noir", the philosopher cat. Each of them is a bit of an internet celebrity in their own right- for example, Cooper's owners regularly attach a digital camera to his collar and let him wander off, letting the camera occasionally taking a picture from a cat's-eye view, and a collection of these ended up in a published book. Each of these famous cats helps to guide Kimchi on his way to finding his lost owner.
Each level also contains things to find- two hundred stinky fish bones have been hidden through each level, along with a kidnapped, caged cat and a collectible that ties in with that level's famous cat- be it a piano score of Nora's music, a copy of Cooper's book, etc. These can be hunted down and found for achievements, just like the kidnapped cats can. The caged cats are kind of hard to find- but if you just keep looking around and listening for the meowing when you get close, you'll be on your way to finding them. Cat scratchers are also littered through each level- touch one of them to save your progress through the level and it'll serve as a continue point.
However, well... not everything is catnip and boxes- Kimchi will have to deal with a selection of enemies through each level. Mice, birds, frogs, pits, spiked fences, sharp-thorned cacti and, of course... dogs. The dogs are the worst- while you are able to attack with a claw swipe while standing still, there's not much you can do against a dog except run away or try to hide. If one catches your scent, the only thing you can do is run away from it and hope it doesn't catch you. If one does, you'll end up losing a hit and be sent back to the last cat scratcher you touched. Kimchi can also lose a hit by falling too far- you'll crash to the ground and be sent back to the last scratcher you passed. Get hit seven times and that's all she meowed- but you have unlimited continues and you pick up at the last scratcher you activated, so death really isn't much of a penalty.
You get to chose between a few different options in the beginning- the game not only supports KBAM, but it also uses a controller no problem. You also get to choose jumping styles- either Kimchi can do a high jump or a double jump, whichever suits your playstyle better.
I completed the game in about an hour, but I imagine that going to find everything (which I plan to do) will expand it to maybe three or four hours.
I only have a handful of complaints about this game- the fish bones you need to collect are only really highlighted with a faint green aura- I'd really like it if they had a bit more color to them so they were easier to spot. Also, there's a rather jarring rhythm game section after the fourth level where you have to play a section from the game's theme song on a four-key keyboard. You get infinite tries to do it, but... the last thing I was expecting was to have to do something like this, and there's no warning or opportunity to practice.
Steam wants ten funbucks for this- and I'd be happy to pay that for this. The graphics are solid, the gameplay is tight and well-made, and there really don't seem to be any major game-breaking bugs. Not to mention that a portion of the proceeds go to animal welfare organizations, so you're helping out animals in need and getting a decent game for playing or gift-a-pulting, which is all good and wonderful.
TL;DR - Buy this game. The cats command it. 8/10.

Retro City Rampage is a pretty straight forward title. It's retro, takes place in a city, and you rampage. This is the game, a majority of the game. Visually, the game hits the mark spot on, colors and and sound design truly do evoke the right feeling. The missions aren't particularly fun, mainly consisting of "A to B while C, then return to A", or "Fill Quota of X" missions. It's an open world, and you can drive. The primary issue with this game is it relies almost entirely on trying to tickle the nostalgia part of your brain and reference things from the 80's. Do you like that? If you do, you might like this game. And in fact, some of the jokes and pokes are humorous, but it feels oversaturated. There's nothing wrong with being an 8-bit style game. But in Retro City Rampage, when you strip away the cheesy reference humor and the old school aesthetic, I feel that you'll find that there's not much worthwhile beyond that.

If you grew up in the 80s, prepare to have most of the pop culture of your generation satirized. Well worth the price of admission as it's done well for those that remember the early console days, and if you came of age in the 80s it really should be in your library. Younger players may find less to draw them in with intentionally and well done retro gaming mechanics, graphics, and audio though.
For what it's worth this gamer gives it 8 out of 10.

Excellent game. I was lucky enough not to get any of the glitches some people have written on forums. Maybe patches had fixed it before i got there? Anyway i most thoroughly enjoyed this game (one i took the time to get all collectables/achievements etc). A totally different gaming experience than the first 2 SGWs. The way you can approach a mission either by stealth, from a distance or COD style and the stragegy involved and different ways to enter the one facility can be challenging. Besides the combat (obviously max prefers his fists or close range weapons) the game is alot like Mad Max in the way you have the main story, side stories/missions and points of interest and collectables also the ability to loot dead bodies/weapons. Also a big similar feature is the open world map.
Graphics are decent and to get a great FPS on high res and max settings you do need a reasonable system.
If you like running around killing as many people as you can in the quickest time possible like in COD and BF (although this is possible in a few missions), this game is not for you. It is definately for someone with a slower trigger finger that enjoys not alerting the enemy they are trying to infiltrate.
Major Con: Without starting a complete new campaign and loosing all your stats, once you have completed a mission you can't go back and do it again, even after you complete the game. I think this is a major design flaw as you may have either missed a "secondary" objective or would like to try the mission from a different approach without loosing your stats. Although note: points of interest and collectables can all be done at the end as after the game has ended, it puts you back in your bunker where you are again free to go where ever in the open world as you have been able to do so at any point throughout the game you just can't do any main or side missions.
Overall i rate it up there amongst my favs but i do enjoy that type of gameplay.

Sniper Ghost Warrior 3 is a surprisingly fun, open world shooter.  It's a big improvement  than the previous games.  Set in Georgia which looks very authentic and atmospheric. It has a very eastern European look, with woodlands, fields, rivers, lakes and villages to explore.  The story is nothing special, so don't buy if you're expecting some epic deep experience, but it does have a lot of dark political realism, dealing with war and conflict.  The graphics are very nice as it runs on the Cryengine, you will require a good PC to run on the Highest settings, but I'm getting over 80fps on this setting so it runs well.
I turned off bullet cam as this was annoying, it has not been done very well, and looks dated compared to Sniper elite 4. However shooting looks great without this option and very satisfying.  You can use a drone to plan your attack and mark targets to snipe. And depending on your skill level sniping can be very complex if you wish it to be. Such as wind adaption, bullet drop and sight acquisition adjustment. There are many side quests, wepons and collectables to collect if you are a completionist too.  This game is not for everyone but if you're looking at the game and your instincts tell you it looks good, you will enjoy Sniper Ghost Warrior 3.

Who remembers the underrated IGI games? Being a big fan of both, SGW3 feels like a true spiritual successor, so this title already tickles my pickle. For those unfamiliar with IGI, imagine a more condensed and realistic version of the Far Cry series without all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.
Let's get this out the way: the game description says "modern military shooter". So no animal hunting, side activities or other such Ubishite nonsense: this is a modern military shooter as mentioned in the description. Want to chase checkpoints or skin animals, go play Far Cry instead: let's not down vote a game because you can't tell oranges from apples.
Been reading people slating the game for having "last gen graphics, bad graphics", etc. You know the doctor was right, doing it too much leads to blurry vision.
Seriously, the game looks gorgeous. Expect to visit many varied locations, from desolate forests, train yards, abandoned apartment blocks plus thankfully sparse appearances of underground labyrinths. The scope (no pun intended) of each level is massive, it's just a shame the draw distance falls short of around 1km.
Texture work is excellent, characters look great and the weapons look phenomenal. Top everything off with an adjustable day and night cycle just sweetens the visual package.
Aside from the strangely appealing menu music, the soundtrack is fairly minimal. Which is a plus, as I want to be able to hear the enemy’s footsteps and farts in this game, not some artificial orchestral or trumpets blowing up my♥♥♥♥♥♥ The soundtrack has been done with intentional restraint, so kudos to CI Games for that.
Many of the guns themselves sound great, echoing plus reverb depending on what environments you’re in, whether you're in a dank tunnel or nestled on top of a hill. Surround sound is done fairly well, and you can often pinpoint enemy locations by the sound of their footsteps alone.
Ambient sounds are decent but tend to cut out completely just by going indoors or in a vehicle (even your buggy). Some interiors are virtually silent and kill the otherwise immersive audio.
Now we come to the dialogue, which seems to get on everyone’s♥♥♥♥♥♥ Yes, it’s not good, but it’s not bad either. It’s just people talking about go here, kill this, steal that. Sure, it’s not going to get an Oscar and there are some very cringe worthy lines, but did you really expect gun welding stone cold mercenaries to perform bleedin’ Shakespeare? No, I didn’t think so.
The game is somewhat semi-open world, allowing you to freely explore the landscape, perform tasks at your leisure or just explore and cause general havoc upon the residents of Georgia.
You get to choose from a varied arsenal of juicy firearms, all boasting individual stats and modelled to perfection. Each weapon can be customised to a varying degree and whilst you are spoiled for choice, the weapon balancing is pretty poor.
I say this because as you unlock weapons in the game, your next gun might perform worst than the previous one, which makes no sense at all! Plus whilst I'm no firearm expert, I was under the impression that a .45 calibre handgun generally causes more damage than a 9mm one, no?
Moving swiftly onto the meat of the game, upon receiving an objective (or not) you head to a location, sneak to various high vantage points generously dotted around the landscape (as enemies love building secret bases below precarious sniping spots) and grin with glee just thinking about all the different routes you can take.
You can use your cute little aerial drone to scout for enemy positions, secret routes and all that jazz. Once you've figured out the lay of the land, you can either start sniping fools, sneak in close for some wet works, or shoot your way through.
As the title suggests, sniping has been given the strongest focus. Since the game features bullet drop and wind speed, you'll have to adjust your scope accordingly to compensate, and there really is something immersive watching your character manually tune his scope click by click. I've found the in-game ballistics to be extremely consistent and missed shots were always because I messed up. The sniping never cheated or trolled me, unlike in Sniper Elite. Finally, sniping done right!
Once you're done picking off snipers and sentries, you can attempt to sneak into the base, hack into CCTV cameras and interrogate enemies for information. The stealth in the game won't rival that of something like Splinter Cell, but it's fairly enjoyable and not too hardcore. Lights can be shot out to cover your approach, stones thrown to distract overly curious guards, and you can climb most buildings and cliff edges... sometimes. Overall, I've found this method of gameplay to be the most enjoyable and brings me back to the days of playing IGI.
So onto the shooting... yea. The standard combat falls short and has been done much better in other FPS games. Assault rifles have the strangest recoil that I've never been able to adapt to, and there isn't much sense in taking anything other than an AK-47 as 99% of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s in the game carry one, and NATO ammo is rarer than rocking horse♥♥♥♥♥♥ Least the enemies aren't bullet sponges.
The AI is somewhat competent: they take cover, flank you and call for backup. They do stupid things sometimes like climbing up ladders one at a time right into your crosshairs, but asides from that they are a challenging force to be reckoned with, at least on hardest difficulty.
I’ve fallen through the world a few times, climbing isn't 100% smooth, and the AI can be nearly godlike: if you miss a single shot, god have mercy on your soul as they’ll all instantly drop their♥♥♥♥♥♥to start accurately firing on your position 200m away and raining mortars on your head.
Enemies disappearing beyond 300m is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t for a sniping game and seriously needs to be fixed, there's no questions about that.
With reports of long loading times, I'm happy to report that first loading takes 20-45 secs on my rig, with subsequent loadings taking mere seconds. Furthermore, the game runs smoothly at around 50-70fps. Obviously, your mileage may vary depending on your specs, so be warned.
SGW3 is far from perfect, and at worst an above average experience. Personally, I believe all the issues with the game have been blown WAY out of proportion. Sadly thanks to us gamers in general, nothing says "I'm edgy" more than joining in on the latest game-hating bandwagon, which sadly SGW3 fell into. This is why we can’t have nice things in the world.
For me, I enjoy SGW3 for being a focused military shooter with no stupid distractions. I enjoy choosing an enemy outpost and either sniping, sneaking or shooting my way into there, regardless if there's an objective or not.
Take this from me: if you’re a mature PC gamer who knows what this game is about and can forgive the rough edges, you’re in for a brilliant time. For everyone else, leave this one and go back to your “AAA” open-world collectathons.
Now if you excuse me, I’m off to have fun and snipe some fools.

Star Wars Republic Commando is such a unique and addicting game that I find it may even rival the Battlefront series.
Basically you are the squad leader of a 4 person squad.
Delta 40
Delta 62
Delta 07
And you, Delta 38. Together, you form the Delta Squad.
You are clone troopers that have been engineered to be the best of the best. You are the future. You are the commandos.
You must strategically command your squad in order to beat back the droid army on various missions across various planets. Something i'd like to mention is that the droids are very tough in this game, while in the movie they seemed like bumbling pieces of metal that could easily be taken down.  Initially I started the game on normal but had to change it to easy because it was too hard. I may re-play the game on medium though. But even on easy, the separatists are a force to be reckoned with and the enemies are remarkably tough. This makes for thrilling gameplay as all the responsibility falls on your shoulders as the squad leader, and you must make hard decisions. In the end, only 2 things matter. Win the battle, and get your squad out alive. But later in the game, you must choose which is more important....
Each squad member has a unique personality, and as the game progresses you feel very close to them.
The members are:
Scorch, (62)
Fixer, (40)
Sev, (07)
And you, 38. Or, Boss.
You are alone, cut off, and all you have is your squad. You do whatever it takes to save them.
I'll never get tired of hearing:
Engage snipe maneuver, Delta.
Rearrange some architecture, commando.
I want some explosives here, Delta!
Stop limping around and get some bacta, soldier.
Engage anti armor position, delta!
Something i'd like to mention is that your character's full number is actually 1138. 38 is just for short. I think that's cool because THX-1138 was a screenplay George Lucas wrote in college. So that's a neat little Easter egg there.
And also, at the end of the game you can hear the x wing pilots from a New Hope saying things they said during the Death  Star run. So that's another cool little Easter egg.
I also like how you can attack your squad, and they fight back! I tried killing my squad mates one time, and found myself fighting against them. I actually felt really bad. XD
This game is spectacular, extremely fun, unique, and a must-buy.
It was so much fun for me because I am a HUGE fan of the Clone Troopers. I just think they're really cool, and being able to not only be one, but be a commander throughout this game, was an incredible experience.
I would definitely, whole heartily recommend this game. The only thing I'm disappointed about is that there isn't more. I thought there'd be several more planets and missions leading up to Order 66. Oh well, maybe there will be a sequel in the future called Imperial Commando. (Just please don't have EA make it)

A little simple for my preferences but I enjoyed seeing all the little pictures and comments and things on the background, and of course, the cats are rendered adorably. The animation is also quite lovely - I enjoyed watching Kimchi slow their descent as they slid down the tiled rooves. I also found it pretty neat how all of the level endings had unique challenges.
I do feel that the controls were a little stiff, feeling it odd that I couldn't swipe in the air. I was also a bit upset by the fall-too-far-and-die thing, as cats are well known for their good landings. I mean, I understand from the skyscraper level, but the others...
I definitely delighted in various little things that could be done - knocking over the coffee cups, sending apples flying, smashing vases - and hope there will be more of that kind of thing throughout levels in future games! I also enjoyed the soundtrack - it felt very fitting in every level. I also like how the menu screen changed as you progressed.
It was quite jarring how the creatures would disappear in a puff of smoke if killed. I also wish there was more to dogs than just being seen and running from their patrol. Another thing is the pushing of objects - quite tedious honestly, though I appreciate that a cat is not going to push a cement block very fast.
I think Snicker has to be my favourite cat in the game, he is beautifully fluffy and looks so happy.
One thing that put me off a bit was Tika's ending speech. This is almost all of what we see of Tika and their explanation for capturing other cats is "because I like being evil" basically. Which sucks the meaning out of being a villain. I feel it could have been more impactful if Tika had been out to have them declawed because Tika felt they were a threat to him, which would bring back the whole "no declawing!" thing and make it more prominent, as well as set purr-spective on the captured cats -despite being maybe disadvantaged one way, that they were still equal to other cats, and hence deserving of the same love, as I feel was a message the game was trying to push (and a great one at that).

I can only tentatively recommend Fight The Dragon as it stands right now.
The game, when it behaves, is fun. Slashing or blasting your way through adventure after adventure is addicting, whether you're running through a new one or coming back to an old favorite for the thirtieth time because it's solidly made. The rewards for doing what the name of the game asks of you are nice, thought the timers are a bit irritating. The Adventure Creation Kit works just fine, as well. Which it should, because that's where Three Sprockets seems to be putting all their attention.
Some weapons refuse to connect. The greatsword is the perfect example; the first two swings tend to miss. A lot. Even if the swing looks like it should have bisected your target. The axe also tends to catch air if you put it half an inch to the side of where the axe thinks it should be. Using these weapons WILL have you taking unnecessary hits. Projectile hitboxes are also an issue, with staff bolts impacting the guy next to your target, or the auto-target clinging to a mook because it happens to be a foot closer to you than your target.
Then there's the platforming. It's weird, sticky, and slide-y. Relatively flat levels won't have the issue, or at least it won't be that noticeable. But, considering that the game is pretty much all community levels - and I won't be speaking to their quality here, it's not the place - there are going to be platforming challenges, even if the level description doesn't advertise it.
Tip: ANGLE THE CAMERA.
Make the jump straight forward. If you don't, there's a good chance you'll just 'walk' on the edge for a bit before the game gets bored and bounces you off into the abyss. Simple things like stairs can either be a little flavor added to a level or a fragmented turd unceremoniously pinched off from the♥♥♥♥♥♥of the Antichrist. You will - WILL, it's a guarantee - see your character fling themselves off into empty air because you turned around on a cliffside and got too close, or be attracted Nathan Drake-style to a climbable ledge precisely when you don't want to be.
If Three Sprockets fixes the above - come on, guys, combat and movement are only TWO-THIRDS OF THE GAME - then I can fully recommend Fight The Dragon. As it stands now, only get it if you can handle the game not doing what you tell it to.

I can't help but love Fight the Dragon.
It's Diablo without the hassle. It's a game with core mechanics so simple you can understand them within minutes. It's you and some friends wading through a challenging adventure which likely none of you have seen before.
If I wanted a deep fantasy RPG with strong characters and a thick plot, I'd go and play Dragon Age. What we have here is something very different – a game that you can pick up and play without all of that traditional RPG baggage. Grab a few friends, hit 'random level', and give it a go. I challenge you not to have fun.

Fallout Tactics is known as the black sheep of the series. For a variety of reasons, some of them justified. This game wasn't designed by Black Isle, instead it was licensed off to third party studios.
Now what I should state is what this game isn't. Fallout Tactics doesn't feature any towns and the game's story is mostly mission based with breaks inbetween to visit Brotherhood of steel bunkers. It also takes place in Illinois, so the original Fallout continuity is also slightly butchered.
However, Tactics is an isometric turn based tactical shooter where you control a squad of soldiers. Your squad is entirely customizeable and all level up like you do. Later on in the game you get access to more unique party members like Super Mutants and Deathclaws. The Tactics in general are very pronounced in this game, and it is very rewarding to complete a mission.
In general I believe it mostly got hate because of the dumbed down spin off nature of the game. But if you go into it not expecting the Fallout 3 we were promised before Black Isle bit the dust, you'll find yourself a fairly decent tactical shooter for a good price.

I really enjoyed this game, once I learned how to play it properly.
So first off, sniping mechanics are awesome and make shots harder when you turn off the aim assistance. Sneaking is your basic stay out of sight and you won't get spotted. The sound mechanics are good, you get spotted if you're too loud, and rifles can be heard from far away. You get a multitude of rifles, machine guns, shotguns, pistols, and (my personal favorite) bows to complete your missions, as well as gadgets. The story is nothing special, but it's just fine if you aren't super finicky about it.
The gameplay itself is only repetitive if you allow it to get repetitive. You have a large variety of weapons and gadgets at your disposal, so use them. Instead of killing everyone with a silenced pistol or silenced AR, make an elaborate trap using a mine and luring devices. Drone out the entire area and figure out where to put mines to kill patrolling enemies. Use a mine to kill someone, and plant another one on their body to kill anyone who investigates. Try sniping everyone with the bow or spray down everyone in your path with an LMG. There's way more that you can do than people seem to be figuring out. The devs put a lot of stuff in the game, so why not use it?
Also, I feel people are reviewing this game much more harshly than it should be for a $30 ($50 with season pass). This isn't going to be the superb, near-flawless, bug-free game that a $60 price tag would command. There will be bugs, there will be glitches, and if you experience one just reload/fast travel if you need to and continue on.

-Great art style. The graphics, the cards, the character. It's pretty good.

Cons
-The multiplayer. There's no one there as far as I can see. Maybe I'm just unlucky or in different time zones but with more people this could be better.
-Also multiplayer. Sometimes everyone just got disconnect and left with only me or I got disconnected. Although that will put AI in the spot but multiplayer gives you loots. Perhaps it's my internet or it's because of the server.
Overall, if you want to find a board gave that has lots of replay value, want to see good art, or just want something fun to play to kill time then this game is for you.

Play the free demo if you're not sure about this game. Factorio is one of those games where you say you'll do 30 minutes of it and then 10 hours later you've redesigned your entire base. You're always telling yourself "I'll do this later" rather than doing it now. You make production lines for factories, mining ores like uranium, coal, oil and iron and eventually processing them into things like fuel, ammunition, vehicles, rockets, walls. Early on in the game you start off with your bare hands and a single inefficient mining drill. You use that drill to get ores for another drill, eventually you have enough ores for a conveyor belt so you can transport to ores instead of running back to manually collect them. Then after a while you'll have enough ores to design a setup so your mining operatrion fuels itself and unloads itself. As the game progresses you'll start learning about electricity via fossil fuels, and learn the values later on about solar energy and battery backups on your power grid. You'll then learn about nuclear energy all the while the rest of your factory is slowly improving in efficiency, size and speed. If you work hard enough, your hard work will pay off and eventually you can have every single aspect of your factory 100% automated so you can leave your PC while your factory runs. The end goal is to launch a rocket with a satelite into orbit which requires a MASSIVE amount of resources and A LOT of time unless your factory is beefy enough to pump out enough parts effectively. You can also get little robots that fly around and transport things and build/repair stuff for you. Which brings me to aliens.. The larger your factory grows, the more pollution you make which makes the surrounding enemy aliens more agressive and stronger who learn and adapt to your base defences and know where all the weak points are. You'll find the aliens immediately attack a section of undefended border, and once inside go straight towards where the heart of your factory is, and that can be whatever. I once had the aliens enter my base because I forgot to make a turret automatically reload itself, and they immediately ran over to my power station. The problem with my power station is that all it required was a single power pole to be destroyed to shut down power to my entire base, and since my automatic turret reloading required electricity, my base became quickly unprotected and aliens rushed in and destroyed my base. In my next playthrough I learned from that mistake, only to have so much pollution and not enough fortification of my defences to match the aliens growing strength that they broke in and this time ran straight over to my main transport belts of iron and destryoed it, thus choking my factory of iron which is one of the most common ores you'll use. Without iron, things slowly started shutting down one by one and eventually my base started failing and it took quite a while to get the pace flowing again once I killed all the aliens. This game is probably one of my best purchases, every single playthrough is different from the last as I've learned from previous mistakes and know better and more efficient ways to do things before they're a problem again. Not only that but even after several playthroughs when you think you've mastered it, there's other gamemodes like expensive mode where everything requires a lot more resources to craft and build. There's a few other game types but I'm still a noob to the game over 100 hours in, so I haven't tried those gametypes yet. Everything you do in this game feels satisfying, achieving and fulfilling, and it's honestly a bit relaxing sometimes to just stop and watch your factory run like clockwork and think.. I built that

-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Another old school Mario 64 type platformer blesses us, with tight controls, addictive item collecting, and greatly updated visuals.
Ty the Tasmanian Tiger
Journal - Entry #1
First, let's get this out of the way. The question on everyone's mind is, what's a Tasmanian Tiger? Is it even real? Is it like a Tasmanian Devil? Do we even care? Well I'm here to tell you without using too much of my sleuthing skills that yes, yes it is real. Well I think so at least. Below is a picture.
I said it before and I'll say it again. Bit.... oops wrong thing. I welcome all games like Mario 64 with open arms now-a-days. Before you couldn't take two steps without one being flung at your head with a frisby like precision headed for your friend at just the right spot (near some good looking people). Now it's like a desert, a barren wasteland with almost none to be found. Poi was a welcome surprise, and next years Yooka-Laylee looks absolutely awesome, one to look out for, for sure. Let's get started.
Ty the Tasmanian Tiger is a remastered version of the original Ty, which came out on the PlayStation 2 on September 10, 2002. I never played it then, but I feel like I'll appreciate it more, now. It's a colorful world with a bright cheery cast of characters. The controls were a little bit too touchy when I first started, but by the end of my short thirty minute play through ( one whole level) I came to get used to it.
Ty has plenty of collectibles. The usual items that are thrown about the level like M64's coins, the more valued item that only appears once a few times, etc. A boomerang is the weapon of choice for Ty, it's a tiny bit annoying, emphasis on tiny, but annoying nonetheless. Why? because there is no lock on mechanic, you position your character towards the enemy and press the action button and it throws it. You can also switch to first person mode, for a more precise way of throwing the boomerang. Seeing as though it's a remaster I can't see why they couldn't add an auto-target feature.
Unlike Mario 64 where there were worlds, Ty is more of the Crash Bandicoot level type, but not completely if that makes sense. I'll explain. Going through a level I noticed that there was a ledge that I could not get to, no matter how many times I tried. While playing through the level, new abilities were introduced, one that gave me the ability to glide. I went back to the unreachable ledge and happily glided to it and collected my coins. Another thing I've noticed is that there are items underwater but currently Ty can only splash about in a panic way when you try to dive. Further adventuring I was awarded a second boomerang. These are fun to throw weapons.
I enjoyed my time with Ty the Tasmanian Tiger, and I hope to lash some faces with my boomerangs and get to my next entry soon. Thanks for reading.

Alright, this game is AWESOME.  Star Wars Republic Commando is an FPS based on the lives of Delta Squad, 4 elite clone commandos who are sent on the most dangerous and imperative missions the republic has to offer.  Each one has his own distinct personality and all 4 of them (you play as squad leader) are pretty likable characters.  Here are the commandos in order:
38 "three-eight" aka "Boss" or "Sir"- the squad leader and the player character. He is fully voiced by Temuera Morrison, the voice actor for Boba and Jango Fett in the films.  38 (said literally "three-eight")  is a no nonsense commander with a head for strategy and a dry sense of humor.  He leads the squad (obviously) and is able to issue orders to the other 3 commandos, for example, he can tell them to set up sniper positions, anti armor, mount turrets, use healing stations, etc.  (btw these are actual game mechanics, issueing orders to your squad is a huge part of the game).  He has all the weapons that the other 3 commandos are capable of wielding but unlike the others he is capable of using special, enemy weapons that can be found off certain foes.
40 "four-oh" aka "Fixer"- Fixer is the tech specialist of the squad and specialises in hacking and computer interfaces, he is very useful for hacking terminals.  While all the commandos have the same skills and abilities, some are better than others at certain things.  For example, Fixer can hack faster than the others, Scorch is more accurate with grenades and can set explosives faster and Sev is a deadeye with a sniper rifle.  Fixer takes his job verrry seriously and doesn't talk about much other than the mission or how to accomplish it, but he does have moments where he loosens up.  Fixer is exceptional at melee combat and dispatches melee using foes with ease.
62 "six-two" aka "Scorch"-  Scorch is the squad demolitionist and explosive expert and his outlook on life relfects that.  He loves danger and has a very positive, optimistic viewpoint on any sitution, using humor to deal with even the most harrowing of missions.  He is the squad funny guy and his upbeat personality is definitely helpful when things look grim.  Scorch's preferred weapon of choice is the anti-armor grenade launcher and grenades themselves.
07 "oh-seven" aka "Sev"-  Sev is the designated marksman and stealth fighter of the squad and revels in war and battle.  He is a deadly sniper and the best shot in the squad (other than the player).  He is probably the most mandalorian out of the squad and by that I mean he lives for war.  62 finds his fervor for killing to be a bit creepy at times but he is a good soldier and a good friend... and a truly terrible enemy.  Sev's weapon of choice is the sniper rifle, which he uses with pinpoint accuracy.
The game's combat is pretty good and the squad AI is amazing even for today, the commandos feel very human and real.  The game even has multiplayer which I'm not sure if there is anyone on it anymore but it was good in its own way as well.
The story is pretty good and involving and gets pretty hectic at times which keeps things interesting.
All in all this is one of the best star wars games out there and I highly reccomend it for any star wars fan.  I know I spent most of this review talking about the characters, but I did so because they are  the game's strongest attribute.

NOT for kids - there is a lot of hardcoded cursing and some pretty considerable violence including realistic blood spattering.  And oh yeah, it is a game about killing each other.
FOR everyone else who ever wanted an adrenaline rush.  There is no HUD.  Depending on the server, there is little to no indication of a hit or even a kill. A lot of times I will wait a long time after shooting someone just to make sure they are dead.  Shooting a corpse has just the right effect too.  It kinda limply moves with the impact.  The game has a serious learning curve.  I see the new players either lamenting the lack of [frankly unrealistic] information.  You get a map feature that does what the entire game does so well.  It gives you information from which to extrapolate what you need to figure out.  But not COMPLETE information.
"I can see that there is a guy on my team at the objective.  Is he on the right floor? Does he see or hear the guy sneakung up behind him?"
It's like the question of did I get that guy.  Shooting the corpse is a strong indicator.  But was that an old corpse or the guy I just shot?  Should I give up my location by chancing the noise of another shot to check?  The whole game is gritty like that.  You can try keeping your gear light to run faster with a well-timed combat slide to make it across the road.  But if the shooter is good, he will get you anyway.  Maybe wait until he reloads to try.  Where is shooting from?  I don't hear the gunfire and I dare not risk peeping around the corner.  Hmm, blood splatter high on the wall.  He is probably lying prone.
Sure, it's a shooter.  But you improve as much by learning not to do stupid stuff as by muscle memory.  You can tell who the noobs are.  They run when they should be walking (I sitll do this too much).  They miss opportunities to crouch behind an obstacle.  They try to use a weapon with a long barrel in a tight spot.  They can't quite understand how to use smoke.  They use the front entrance/exit. etc.
I see that it is $1.49 right now.  My last starbucks was like $6.00.  That would make this the best investment on enjoyment/entertainment in my life.

Hit 100 hours of play and MP level 10 in this game today. Not sure if this is a bad thing. Ok, yes, I am totally enchanted by this game, please send help.
The setup of the game is a combo of Game of Thrones, Redwall and classic fairy tales. A group of heroes race to take the throne from a corrupted king. Artwork is not too cartoonish, stiff, furry, or overdone. The gameplay is simple, fun, dynamic and (relatively) balanced.
But, honestly? The best about this game is the character design. Each hero is archetypal, yet unique. Their stats/inclined win conditions fit their character and complement one another.
It's SO freaking refreshing to see female characters not be even remotely sexualized in a game. Take Elyssia, Twiss and Magna.  All three are women, but that fact is completely irrelevant to their personalities, motivations, abilities, emotes and visual design. As a trans/queer person, seeing this sh*t means the world to me.
You're never going to play the same game of Armello twice. The key to enjoying a game is understanding which heroes are best suited for certain win conditions, take into account your opponents character/win inclinations, start with that in mind and be ADAPTABLE as the game changes over time.
I don't play a lot of other MP games because pvp players tend to be just plain nasty. I've hardly ever experienced this while playing Armello. The only way a player can communicate with opponents is with emotes and in-game actions, and players who intensely antagonize others usually end up getting ganged up on by the remaining 3. In order to win, you need to strike a healthy balance between persuing your own win condition, undermining players who get in your way, undermining the player who has the best shot at winning the fastest, and knowing when to call truces. If you get too caught up in fighting others, a wiser pacifist is going to sneak in and steal the victory. You've got to play nice, play smart, and above all play to win.
Rolling for the Chest/Keys after a MP game can get frustrating, but we've got to understand that LOG is a pretty small (maybe 10 person?) company that is always working to improve the game. They've got to make money, so we get nickled and dimed. imo, there are more important things to get mad about in the gaming industry
A lot of folks are going on about how you need the DLC characters to win. This blatantly isn't true. From my experience, the level 60+ seasoned players who nearly always win love to go for River Brun and Sana. I will say that the abilities of the DLC characters are a lot more fun to mess around with than the base set, (unpopular opinion: I love Sargon) and add a lot of dimension to the game play and various win conditions. My personal hero pics are Elyssia > Sylas > River > Sargon > Magna.
Anyways, do yourself a favor and have fun with this game!

If Grand Theft Auto was made on the NES, this is what it would play like. Retro City Rampage features a fairly expansive open world with the car-theiving fun of GTA and the tongue-in-cheek humor of Nintendo games of the past. It revels in fact that it is a parody and makes every effort to remind you of it. There are enough 80's and 90's references to fill a hundred parodies, so don't even bother trying to figure out all of the source material.
I was surprised by how many unlockables there are in this game and finding all of them proves to be quite the challenge. You can also customize your character with hats and hairstyles. For me, this really put RCR as more than just a parody. It's a love letter to two very different eras of gaming that go surprisingly well together. Some of the challenges are pretty frustrating, but even that difficulty harkens back to a time gone by of gaming. Even after you've done everything there is to do, there is still some sick fun to be had by running over pixelated people with the Ghostbusters car.
