State of Decay is a fabulous game.
Thrown into a very vanilla zombie apocalypse, the game doesn't offer much new here.
What is incredible is the interaction with other survivors, some which you can take into your community.
You are able to swap between characters, and PHYSICALITY is a massive past of State of Decay.
If you run, you get tired. If you fight zombies, you get tired. If you carry too much, you get really tired. If you stay out on runs too long, you get tired.
Managing this limited and precious resource of stamina is a huge part of the game. Frequently the game throws high risk and high reward situations at you.
And this game has perma-death.
For example the other evening I was using my main character Maya to do a run across the other side of the map. Maya is my fave character, and has the best stats which I have developed over time.
Maya had a to-do-list including some supplies, a Zed hunt (which helps your neighbors and builds influence), and finally a run deep back to the starting area to recover an item for a friend in the camp.
Everything was fine until I got to the final stage.
Doing such a long run, I had not left enough stamina for Maya when she needed it most. Crossing a river she got caught in the middle of two hordes, and her life was nearly taken.
She limped out of that engagement with no meds, a couple of rounds of ammo and only one molotov remaining.
What followed was a very tense walk to the destination which was fraught with fear over running into another horde.
Then at the destination she found an infestation, which is a big bad ugly mess of zeds.
To turn around and go home, resupply, and switch to another hero would have been the smart and safest thing to do.
Maya went in, dispatching half of the zeds with the molotov.
She got mauled by a few zeds, pushing her health into the last 25%, and contemplated running for it.
Her stamina was gone. Then her primary weapon broke.
There were two zeds left, but a horde outside had already started to engage.
Maya finished off the two zeds from the infestation and then dove out a back window, limping her way to a watchtower where she could hopefully get her breath back.
Everything went quiet. The zeds dispersed. Maya picked them off one by one silently in the dark, went back and recovered her item.
Then she had to get back to the car.
She got to within 100 yards when another horde revealed itself between her and salvation.
Waiting for every last pip of energy to get into her bar, she bolted for it, evading the zeds and got into the vehicle.
Screaming the tires up the road a radio message tells me that one of my runners is in trouble, and may die without assistance.
Just one more mission before I can get her home...

I dug deep into this game as soon as I got it. It's really driven and entertaining at first. I recognize a sandbox game will run out of missions and variety sooner or later, that isn't a problem. Actually secretly I love games like the old school Total Annihilation that I could set up a base, leave it overnight, and see if it survived against whatever the enemy threw at it. This one fell slightly short of that, as zombie attacks on the base were really... non-threatening. Venturing out most definitely was. And if you didn't go out, your housemates had a good chance of tearing each other apart with negative events.
I'd like to have a little more control over what my characters do. At the start it's fine to not be leader but as you get more and more in charge there should be a sort of command or planning system to decide who and when go where etc etc. With a little AI help and some personality of course. The repetition after clearing all the little factions became a bit much.
Aside from that, yes there's a few bugs. Nothing that bothers me too much. And the special infected do throw you for a bit of a loop. Running over one of those spoogers can virtually kill you in a car. And the fat one. Well damn. Killing those take a ton of firepower or half of an SUV.
My biggest gripe though was how whoever I influenced to join me on a run would leave anytime I reached a mission area. I mean FFS, that's why I brought them in the first place. I don't expect to be able to issue them commands or the like, but there was just no point to having any company unless you're going to non-mission, in which case the expired missions tear the community apart.
Saw a lot of graphics and etc comments. Yes the graphics aren't stellar. But neither are half the pixel games that are also really fun. I had some frame lag especially while driving that did hurt, but I have a slightly older machine so that's expected. So nothing to say there really except if you want top of the line, go get top of the line.

In a game with permanent deaths, there's no room for bullsh't.
If you buy this, you'll be disappointed to see there's plenty bullsh't to go around in there. It's too hardcore, too tiresome, too sprinkled with errors for me to recommend it.
That said, before I go on tearing this game as many holes as it deserves, gotta say it's a pretty solid game. I can tell it's NOT made by immature re't@rds; but in the end it all boils down to how easily the game gets your characters permanently killed, without it even being your fault, after you spent several hours, perhaps even days on them.
I can only recommend this to professionals who'd wish to see how close these guys got to making a solid hardcore zombie-outbreak team-survival base-building scavenging type of thing. For everyone else, permanent character deaths should have been an *optional* feature. That'd make the game errors and other shenanigans at least more bearable.
On the technical side of things, the game runs with some performance issues though it seems to be an *anti* system-resource-smothering application designed to run on limited resources, just seems to choke itself while unloading-loading chunks. Nothing on the scale of outright unacceptable though.
~~~~~~~~~~~~~
~~Game errors~~
~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Like when you walk up to a zombie and hit space to kick it but your character jumps instead like there's no zombie, then gets grabbed and bitten...
Like when you go up some stairs to survey the place, like up a water tower, and your way back down your character doesn't feel like holding onto the stairs and just dies...
Like your firearm's range is so low, you keep firing at an lpg tank and nothing happens, and keep walking towards it and keep shooting until it blows up (normally takes one shot) by which time the game deems you were too close to the thing and it takes 50hp off, possibly killing you...
Like when you've just done a quest with one of your survivors that tagged along you as an npc, and after he/she leaves you, you see em running up to a horde on the way back home and get grabbed... They're stupid like that. They just run towards home without any care for what they're running into.  If you run towards there to help em, they get in an event type of thing, ask for your help and in 3-5 secs they usually just die. The game doesn't let them die on their own if you're far away because the designers obviously knew how stupid that is, but if you go to help they'll definitely die.
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
~~The game cheats to get you killed~~
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
After a few hours you'll be used to how the game usually does things.
In 10 hours you'll be pretty used to how the game sometimes turns on abnormal spawns trying to get you killed.
In 30 hours, you may see your main *god-like* character getting killed in 5 secs by an invulnerable feral, while doing the same stupid "help hunt a feral" quest you've done a hundred times. I've seen that happen twice, once my main character was the npc in that quest, and once I was in control but the game just turned off my controls while it said "keep hitting c to break free" which just didn't work. Ofc then I had hit esc and quit the game before I died, but the second time... My main character was the npc, I showed up to help him hunt a feral with another survivor. Found it, my main turned his back to the feral and got pounced, I shot the feral 5 times, it didn't budge, I smacked it in the head twice, didn't budge, obviously was invulnerable and my main guy's remains dropped on the ground. I knew I should have hit esc and quit before that happened. That's the only way to stop it when the game pulls that bullsh't.
I've seen the game spawning 3 hordes on me and a feral to get me killed (I've seen a feral spawn like that 2 meters from me after the game was done spawning 2 hordes.. it doesn't even have the *decency* to spawn that sh't behind me where I can't see it happen and go like look at that bullsh't...)
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
~~Less potent annoyances~~
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Vehicle mechanics are not ideal, their movements are weird, they get damaged too easily too fast.
Survivors get grabbed too easily; but getting free is rather hard and by taking too much damage.
Every special movement, whether it works as expected or not, costs you stamina. Sometimes the stamina cost builds up to be too much when the game keeps on failing to perform what you're trying to do, specially when you're pitted against such numerous enemies as if the game's trying to have you meet your match, or your doom. Controls and stamina costs could be designed better so that players wouldn't end up wasting stamina jumping in the air (which is good for nothing) instead of fly-kicking zombies (which seems to be the only thing that *always* knocks zombies down).
Even the biggest bases aren't big enough to let you build everything, it forces you to choose, like either choose vehicle repairs or ammo and explosives production...
In case you want to keep playing hours at a time, the game generates an endless stream of problems for you. You end up dealing with characters getting stranded all the time, they ask for an escort, or a distraction for zombies. They go outta your base and keep asking you to help them kill some special zombies... They get depressed, angry, fearful etc etc.. Their morale always go down down down unless you're there holding their hand. As if you're the only capable individual among all those.. meatbags -.- They don't ever let you do your own thing, or enjoy the scenery...... ever!
The characters you control yourself get *tired* pretty fast, which means their max stamina get reduced more and more until you let them rest. This makes you spend a lot more time doing pretty much the same thing developing more or less the same character over and over again with all your survivors, after you're done exploring the easiest skillset to survive ofc. Btw you choose a skill - you're stuck with it for life. You can't start over, can't say I don't like this I wanna pick another...
Some abilities do not work as advertised, like there's this powerful push ability that's supposed to *always* knock the zombie down, but it just doesn't.
Some other errors like some zombies getting back up, with their face back on, to bite you after you just caved in their skulls or watched their heads explode.
(...work in progress...may get additions later...)

A fun little hack-and-slash dungeon crawler. The game features procedurely generated dungeons full of various traps, enemies, and shrines. TinyKeep has a very simple left-click-to-attack right-click-to-defend playstyle and relies upon its randomness (both of the shape of the dungeons and various abilities that can be collected) for replayability. At the time of writing this, I have about 5 hours of playtime and have only played about half of the game. Following the idea of 1 dollar = 1 hour of playtime, this game should suffice. All-in-all, the game is a fun little dungeon crawler worth buying (especially if it's on sale).
Weak combat, repetitive dungeons and lacking in mechanics and content. This is not a good game. Oh, and have fun getting stuck on every single object in the dungeon, no matter how tiny.

I wouldn't say TinyKeep is a perfectly polished and glitch free game but the 2.3 hours I've played it were fun to play, and I still want to play more.
First I'll mention what I like about TinyKeep.
-high difficulty. This one is very important to me since I like games in which the character faces very bad odds. This gives me a little adrenaline rush. The way enemies attack manages to give variety because they vary in size. A number of them could have spawned in one place which forces you to run away.
-Cool traps. I think the traps I've seen so far are pretty cool because they are not only a danger to you but you can lead the pursuing enemies into those areas.
-Random reactions from people you rescue. They might decide to help you. They could be useful. They could be weak and get killed right away. Some will run away and not help you. Then there are some who'll actually attack you. This makes freeing other prisoners a gamble, which I like.
-limited gold and treasure. I like how you are not able to simply farm same areas and collect infinite amount of gold to eventually buy anything you want. At least at the beginning the gold is not common enough to allow you to buy something really fancy. Add to that the fact that you won't always be able to access a seller, so that causes to make decisions that will often decide when your character dies.
-nice cute graphics. I like that the graphics run well on my crappy computer. The design of the dungeons and enemies along with sound makes them all kind of entertaining. I am not as happy about limited options you get to design your own characters.
Cons:
it is important to point out some annoyances and glitches I've seen as well.
-While exploring the different maps that were generated each time I've seen areas where one unbreakable and unpassable object blocks pathways of the doors. Not happening very often but when it does I have to restart.
-AI is pretty weak. Enemies often rush after you despite being near death, or go into the trap without any pause. They often do it in a straight line, which looks very distracting.
-Too few options for character appearance. Would be nice to give them more body options.
-When you encounter the store you might have just a few coins short of some expensive item. Unfortunately the stores usually do not have alternative ways to spend money on cheaper support items like potions, arrows, bad weapons. etc.
Overall I really enjoy the game despite lack of polish or the annoyances. It could be much better if more updates came out.

This game is fun. The map editing program is extensive and I spent a while making some complicated maps. The game is very basic, you gain levels by playing either creator made maps, your maps or maps of other users and eventually defeat the dragon.
Pros:
Map making is easy and fun, and you can accomplish a good amount in a short time.
The gameplay is pretty fluid, although sometimes when you try to hit an enemy with a sword nothing happens. That could just be a miss on the attack, but it isn't indicated.
The loot system reminds me of Borderlands.
The dragon is VERY tough to beat. After pouring several hours into leveling up and getting good gear to fight the dragon I've still only been able to knock out a few thousand health from it per battle. It starts out with a million health, but health doesn't regenerate in between battles, so the damage you do to it is permanent. If you get health regenerating equipment and are willing to run around the map for about 48 hours to avoid attacks while you heal, then you could beat the dragon in one sitting, but I do not recommend you try.
Cons:
Once a moderator accuses your map of being an exploit, it seems they never go back to unban it after you edit it. For example, I built a map that was a straight shot from beginning to end with a couple hundred rats and skeletons to fight. It was by no means an easy map. I would usually beat it with just a single life left. Because of Its simplicity it was banned for being a grinding exploit, and now that I edited it to include Minotaurs (which easily knock a player off my map, thereby increasing the difficulty greatly) It's still in review.
Although bugs are fixed quickly and little things are added here and there, no real new content has shown up to my knowledge since my purchase of the game a few months ago. The game's replay value sinks quickly after you unlock your final ability and realize the only thing you have left to do is suffer through endless generic hours of gameplay to get a bit stronger to stand up to the dragon better.
You can't just go and challenge the dragon whenever you want. You need a scroll, and to get it you need to play a new map. If you don't have an internet connection, you will run out of scrolls quickly and won't be able to play the main purpose of the game.
Overall, the game is good, and I recommend it if you're willing to do the same thing for a while in order ot beat that pesky dragon, and if you're willing to put up with moderators banning you for exploiting, then not giving you a second chance. Don't mess up in map editing, or you'll end up like me, the evil Bonticune.
Things I'd like to see:
A multiplayer option to fight the dragon with. Maybe a dragon whose health resets after each battle, and some prize system if you do a certain amount of damage.
Different equipment when you deal enough damage to the dragon. The time limit rings are good for the few minutes you get them, but the rings that last for even as high as an hour and a half are gone a lot quicker than people would think.
A difficulty higher than extreme. I like heavy combat in my games, and with health regen equipment the game has become too easy.
The ability to have bosses speak before they attack.
The field of views for enemies increased (if the player makes it so while editing)

After you launch your first rocket in Factorio, you remember these last few days that you did not get out of your house, and realize how much better this life is.
At some point later, you will find yourself launching a few rockets per minute. You take one of your trains to commute to the North base, because that damn train ran out of fuel again. While travelling, you check on different parts of the base that need upgrades. You fix that misconnected pipe again, and your fleet of robots takes care of it. You remember, that after this train, the third nuclear reactor array needs some fixing (but you don't care, as you have redundant reactors anyway).
You still haven't arrived to your destination. Since you have some spare time to waste, you decide to play that game called "shopping for food" that requires too many manual crafting operations. If only you could automate that!
10/10

Factorio catches the essence of automation: innovation that serves reduction of human labor.
I think this game is the first and so far one of the only two games (the other is Production Line) that gives you a satisfying experience of creating detailed industrialized assembly lines.
You crash on a hostile alien planet, gather resources to survive, but instead of exhaustively doing everything with your bare hand, you build tools, machines, factories. The overall gameplay feels a bit like 2D version of minecraft with actually working machines mechanism. Tech trees are beautifully designed, which mimics the very core mechanism of each major technological revolution since 18th century industrial revolution. For you crash on the planet alone, you are on your own, not unlike those half slave owner capitalists, so the game force you to exploit the benefit of automation. You yourself shall percieve the whole process of human indutrulization while shooting nauseated worms (I mean indigenous life). You will experiment efficent factoy layout and logistical system, brush up your knowledge on logic gates (or redstone folk science), and ultimately reinvent yourself as a fine engineer.
Remember those satisfying moments of watching videos of pharmaceutical production lines? Now you get to make one of those, and, just watch them.
O now, bow down, nature.

let me preface this by admitting i got this game as a gift from a friend, but only because i was literally to poor to afford it at sale price. I hadn't bought it before simply because i didn't know much about it and was simply going by word of mouth that it was a good game.
That being said, however, I would definitely pay full price for this game (maybe even $30-$40 for a graphical overhaul version)
this game, alongside other titans of the star wars series such as battlefront I & II (before DICE) is easily ne of the best games of it's time and will be an iconic standout, at least to me. the fact that this game even runs on my machine is a marvel, considering it's not even rated for windows 7 on a good computer and im runing it on a piece of trash with windows 10, another piece of trash. Many other reviews have mentioned bugs and crashing, this is simply because their V-Sync wasn't implemented well and the resolution needs to be changed through console commands to work properly(albeit they souldn't have to deal with these issues, they are not complex and im sure you can figure it out, if not the forums exist). on the topic of addressing complaints: the AI is a bit dated, but we're talking like Call of Duty MW3/BO2 era AI here, so i'm not really seeing and issue for this game. Literally any other game i've played from this era has left me agast at how one-sided ad flat the AI is and how unable it is to interact with the player and adapt to new requests. The only real issues i had with the AI was the occasional "oh hey imma switch cover i hope no one is throwing a grenade at my back on the way over."
Stability wise, the game never once crshed during gameplay and, barring particle effect stress on my APU, I had a constant 50+ FPS. with particle effects however, I did dip into the 20s but nothing below that, and this is on a 1.4 GHz 768 MB quad-core A8 5540M APU from AMD, so i can almost guarantee you will have a better experience than i did.
gameplay wise, the game was excellent for tactical squad-based combat, and instilled mre of a reliance on actual planning than more modern games that use squad based gameplay. the game also has a decent variety of enemy types that will provide added difficulty or a nice peaceful grind, depending on the section of the game you are in.
on the topc of enemy variety, it is true that there are not many enemies used within the game itself, but the game does an excellent job of organizing and pacing the enemies you encounter, and also provides plenty of reason for why x group is with y group and why you aren't fighting z group. the enemies also come with a wide variety of classes, ranging from the piddly battle droid to massive spider droids, and so on.
on the topic of graphical fidelity, this game i an absolute marvel that they even got it to work on machines with the minimum requirements so well. despite and obvious low poly count, this game provides a wide variety of hi-res textures and strategic use of low-res textures, so as to not highlight them and say "hey look how bad this is" (albeit the last part kinda throws that out the window, you'll have to play and see). This game also introduces physics in an amazing way, however the ragdolls feel a bit floaty (not quite Dark Souls bad, but you get the drift).
i give this game an easy 10/10 for it's era, but for today, not considering the sale price or that I got it free, this game gets an easy 8.5/10, maybe a 9.

Probably one of the most charming and innovative little games i have ever come across. Fight the Dragon allows it's players to develop an RPG style character while at the same time, building their own worlds/levels and even allowing you to share your own and play other people's levels. The artwork style is very very attractive and the game runs great. It will take anyone a little while to grasp some of the mechanics of the level builder but within the hour you'll be cruising along setting traps, spawning trolls and building towering castle walls. The building style is essentially Minecraft but with a blank canvas and on a much grander scale. Sadly however the community hasn't really kicked off as of yet so youre looking at only 1500 content creators. 9/10 and i hope this game gets more publicity.

I was honestly surprised that I liked this game as much as I do. This game is very derivative of games such as Far Cry 3/4 and Sniper Elite, but I think it handles itself really well. It's much like the way Salt and Sanctuary or Nioh is to the Soulsborne series.
The writing is wonky, but that's excusable because English isn't the developers' first language. It kind of reminds me of an 80's B-Movie in terms of how the script works. If you liked movies like Stallone's Cobra, then this won't seem too bad by comparison. I mean, seriously, that movie had some really, REALLY awful lines in it.
I've been told my taste is really weird/bad a lot in my life, but I still feel like if possible, I'd like let people know that this game isn't as awful as some people say it is. It's definitely not as refined as those other games I mentioned before, but you also have to keep in mind that this game has only a fraction of the budget, team size and combined developer experience of those other titles. For a title of its size, they did a really great job. Just because it looks like a AAA-budget game on the surface doesn't mean that it should be judged the same as one.
Overall, the game isn't great, but I'm having a pretty good time with it so far and will likely continue to for the near future.

The first thing to know and keep in mind about Armello is that it is in fact a board game. As a huge fan of dungeon crawlers this game appeals to me, greatly. You're going to figure out how to fight, you're going to figure out how to avoid traps and you're going to learn to use your surroundings to your advantage when you can. My only real complaint is that the mini-map is crude, blocks your view when used, and just a couple added indicators on it would make navigation a bit easier.
PROS:
+Easy to pickup and play
+Reasonable learning curve
+(Mostly) Random level generation
+No micro-managing inventory
+Achievements are fun additions and realistic to obtain
+Controller support
CONS:
-Mini Map has very little detail
-Mini Map blocks your view when used
-Camera setup takes some getting used to

This has so much potential to be brilliant but it falls just short of ascending. The Characters have a Nintendo quality that is familiar and charming. The hack/slash block jump/run are fairly standard controls. They get more responsive as the game progresses but at no point do they evolve into more complicated moves. You're stuck just hacking away... it gets a bit repetitive and at higher levels, outright boring.
I picked it up for $2.50. For what it is, it's brilliant fun. Levels 1-4 are fairly straight foward, The monsters don't vary too much after that- the bosses are kinda disappointing in that they behave just as regular monsters do- come at you swinging wildly.
_______________
Now for what it could be, that's a whole different story. Add a fighter class with a great axe, a wizard class with a staff, an Elven thief with a bow and a viking Princess with a spear and make it all multiplayer and we'd have the Gauntlet we wanted instead of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t gauntlet we got. I love the monster gates tearing open and streams of enemies attacking both other enemies and the player- it adds a great deal to the environment when you can sieze the opportunity and wait till the weaker baddies weaken the tougher baddies. The four icons lined up slaughtering a horde of fire breathers would be tons of fun...
But we didn't get any of that. We got a single player Gauntlet. It's fun. It doesn't take a great deal of commitment. Doesn't demand a great deal of attention- it just clocks time. It's not disappointing at $2 bucks- I'm not walking away feeling cheated- but after seeing what it is and what it could have been,.. I'm left wanting the later.

It's a pretty simple hack and slash RPG. Choose a class (amongst the four classes), name the character, voila you're ready to start. I like the unique concept of the gold shrine. You can either donate equipments to the loot shrine (essentially selling them) and getting gold in return. As your gold amont increases, the rank of loot increases giving you superior ranked (not necessarily great depending on what you are building your character towards), stat point, health (don't underestimate this, it's an extremely important perk like in any RPG game), bag slot, and so on. Not to mention if you always wanted to create your own custom map for games, this game provides that very feature. I have been having a blast at the start but the gameplay gets pretty dull after for awhile because the game starts heading towards the usual grinding and farming for gold coins to sell and donate respectively to the loot shrine and get equipments and perks from it.
What would be nice to see in future updates are new features such as more specialised classes (like monk, ranger/archer/battle mage, etc) more variety of weapon classes (like bows, knuckles/dusters, fighting staff, etc), more unique features like the ones implemented (loot shrine custom maps, and etc), and if possible a skill tree for all characters so that we can choose what skills we would want therefore allowing us to create a style suited to individuals instead of the fixed 4 skills.

13 hours in and I'm having a BLAST playing this game. Unless you're a "sniper game only, please" kind of player, you will find this game enjoyable. The weapons, the snipers, the CQC is just bada$$. Personally, I'd rather sneak up on some hostiles and eliminate them how I want than to go keep climbing towers to unlock maps. Just saying. This game is a nice mix between something like the Stalker games and the Far Cry series. There's no crazy mutants or pseudodogs to worry about, just human monsters. The CryEngine shines in this game and you can most definitely tell the devs put in some solid hours creating this world. Everything is amazingly detailed. Everything from enemy bases to the smallest log cabin you may come across. From terrorist to Separatist hostiles kidnapping families and murdering them.
Sound design is second to none. Honestly, the sound is awesome. Everything from the pitter patter of the rain to storms to the sounds of the wolves in the wilderness stalking you to the crunching of snow under your feet. Weapon sounds are as expected. AK sounds like an AK. TAC sounds like a TAC. Weapons, scopes, and armaments are detailed and fully functional as well.
I'll be honest, half the fun is exploring this wide open world the devs have created and finding the little nooks and crannies where the bad guys are laying low and taking them out. The missions are superb but the side missons are as much as fun well.
If' you're not a "purist" as far as your sniper games go, I'd go so far as to say this is better than the Sniper Elite series. By a mile. While Sniper Elite 4 is pretty rocking, the pure fact that the devs went the extra mile so you could enjoy gunplay across a wide spectrum of weapons is pretty awesome.

The downside is that the actual gameplay gets very repetitive, very fast. It follows the model of point-and-click style games,  with puzzles involving scouring the area, looking for the item you can pick up and place where needed to advance onward. There's also certain sections that have a "Guitar Hero"-like rhythm mini-game, which was cool the first few times, but got old fast. The slow pace of the gameplay makes the whole experience drag on a lot more than it really should.
Ultimately, there's a really great WWI story and visual novel here, that's bogged down by gameplay that's just too repetitive and slow to make it worth it. If you're super into WWI history, to the point that you're willing to force your way through the gameplay, then go for it. But otherwise, you can skip.
EDIT: Forgot to mention, as others have, that this game requires Uplay, and ♥♥♥♥ everything about that.

Life goes on.

I like what this game aims to do, and I like that it exists, Via its story and memorabilia it offers trivia and information about WWI and how the soldiersa and the rest of the world (well most countries involved anyway) dealt with it. And it has good music/ soundtrack and I like its art style a lot.
Unfortunately, the game's gameplay ruins all that for me. There are a few nice moments and some interesting puzzle solving but the UI, most actions scenes (drive through falling bombs and mines!, run through bombs!, dig through planted and falling mines!, well they are terrible. They make the game frustrating and they disctract from whatever mood it was trying to set.
There is also a particular mini-game for which you get zero turotial, works only with the arrow keys (so you are screwed if you were using WASD up to that point. This mini-game continues throughout the game at many occassions and of course it becomes harder and harder, and if it was no fun the first time, it's way worse later on.
The game has collectibles. The info associated with those is nice. The way some of them are hidden and become challenges or part of puzzles is idiotic. I wanted to get them all, because I enjoyed the trivia, but that made me hit "Space" almost everywhere and destroyed all game's pacing.
Furthermore, the game likes to kill you in unexpected ways, for you to "learn" what to do. I don't particularly like this design decision.
Last, the story is ok-ish and has good moments but ultimately it is dissappointing. The game does something in the end that I am very opposed to, when I see games do it,, but it also pulls a lot of fake cliffhangers so much to the point that they become predicable and tiresome. In the end, this imaginary and imaginative story had better play out constistently either as a tragic story or a bed time story. It attempts to do both and in my opinion it fails when it tries to switch to "serious" mode for its finale.
In the end, I would not recommend this game. It is great that this title exists, and is published by Ubisoft, but there are too many flaws to ignore, and the aftertaste the gameplat left to me was a bad one.

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!
I bought this game on sale but honestly, I think it's worth the full asking price.
the game is just fun and plays really well.
The environment can be interacted with in unique ways that can screw you over or put you at an advantage over the enemy.
The gameplay is simple and addicting and the character models are really funny and cute.
The biggest pro I see in this game is how easy it is to attack and block. When you swing your weapon to attack but realized you should have maybe blocked, it's very forgiving in letting you cancel the attack to perform that block action.
The only real con I think worth noting is the lack of character animations in general. You have run and sprint. I feel like for a game that relies on it's physics and environment, having the appropriate animations for walking, turning and straffing could add a lot more immersion to the experience.
that and it sometime's feels congested trying to navigate the cooridors and dungeons.
People complain about the lack of depth, but I think it's more designed to be a quick pick up and play sort of game. I don't want to have to manage inventory and loot, there are enough games like that. This game takes a more arcade approach to the dungeon crawling experience and that's fine by me.
The game feels like a real lite, simplified 'Gauntlet Legends' experience, but it really isn't anything like that.
All in all, I like the game, I like the simplicitiy of it and I see a lot of potential to improve upon what the developer aimed for in the playing experience.

A streamlined ARPG with addictive gameplay with all the levelin' and lootin' love you could want.
What you will find in FtD:
• Thousands of user-made quests.
• Tons and tons of loot.
• Four varied characters to choose, customize, and level.
• Speaking of customizing, you can do that A LOT in this game.
• Quest creator included which is easy to learn and opens the door to hours of game design fun!  It's like having unlimited Legos to crete an adventure for people to enjoy.
• Multi-player madness at its best. Add friends, multipy the fun.
• Casual gaming without losing much of the more hardcore things like looting and leveling.
• A varied, if somewhat inconsistent, difficulty.
• A low price tag,
• Regular updates by Devs.
• A fight with a dragon you must enter all alone.
What you won't find in FtD:
• Not a very deep character creation system. It revolves more around the loot you get as each class comes with predetermined abilities.
• A story. There is no story to this game. no story mode. Each quest may or may not include a story within itself or as part of a series of quests ("campaigns")
• Top-of-the line graphics. The graphics have a style that reminds me of detailed and well-animated Legos.
• PvP
• Crafting
• Pay-to-Anything schemes, in-game stores, or micro transactions.
The most important thing to know about Fight the Dragon is that it's addictive, hack and slash fun.

Just from a singleplayer side of things, this is very satisfying in terms of small squad real time stealthing.
Perhaps my memory is fading, but this is nowhere near the brutality of Syndicate. Nor is it overly complicated in trying to figure out your upgrades, balanced with weapon choices, balanced with augmentations and gear, balanced with timer limits per mission. All your balance choices are pretty straight forward.
Once you get the hang of it, it's fairly easy, just a matter of playing the waiting game to either wait out patrols, or provoke a redeployment of troops within restricted mission areas by feeding hijacked persons into the meat grinder of death, or blowing something up to get the grunts running in that direction.
The game does have it's glitches and a few dumb AI moments. But some of those dumb AI moments are also useful and can be used as part of your strategy.
The vivid scenery adds more life to the game than Syndicate ever had. But the trade off is it also lacks the hardcore, bleak vibe intended by a world run by corrupt ultra-corporations.
In short though, this game only holds appeal to those that are into squad RTS'ing. Direct reference to Syndicate and the Commandos games. If you didn't like those titles, or thought they were too hard.. this is not the game for you.
And if you haven't played those games... there is one universal rule to this game, like those other titles mentioned.. full on assault will result in guaranteed failure. This game is about stealth, sabotage, theft and assassination. That's it. This ain't a rootin tootin marine corp "I play CoD in my sleep mofo"kill everything head on experience.

Full disclosure: I loved Syndicate and Syndicate Wars is a contender for my favourite game ever.
If you're old enough to have played those games and enjoyed them then this is more of the same - just modernised somewhat.
This game is a bit fiddly and definitely has an indie feel to it. In particular the AI and controls could do with some finessing. If you can get this game on sale for anything under $10 then I suggest it's worth it. If you're a Syndicate fanboy from the 90s like me then it's worth it anytime.

This "game" is a tech demo. It looks really great, and the atmosphere is awesome. The gameplay is frustrating and not worth your time. The game basically forces you to micro-manage operatives and play stealthily but doesn't provide the tools or functionality to do it.
Cons:
-There is an emphasis on stealth gameplay, since attracting any guard will attract basically all the guards/soldiers/drones in your district and overwhelm you. This is extremely difficult to survive.
-Stealth gameplay sucks. Enemies often spot your HIDDEN operatives, and enemies path RANDOMLY which means patrols cannot be predicted and that you can easily get trapped by them. See the previous point for why this is a problem.
-You cannot save while in the middle of a heist/mission. If you are "trespassing" in a restricted area, you cannot save the game. This means your 30 minutes of progress can be thrown out the window in an instant. Expect this to happen ALL THE TIME.
-There are big gameplay issues in regards to bugs. I'm talking about operatives being STUCK IN WALLS OR ON TERRAIN and no way to get them out.
-Operatives will also path poorly if not micromanaged.
-No operative AI, and the combat has no intricacies. Your operatives will not shoot back at enemies, and do such insignifficant damage that you have to focus your whole team on one guard at a time. Combat is so deadly that flanking isn't advisable (guards will continue to join combat from random directions)
Maybe it's more realistic, but its not fun to play. It's too clunky.

The first BitRay was a modest, relatively mediocre 2.5D physics puzzler that was brief enough to not overstay its welcome or let its flaws overshadow the bite-sized chunks of fun on offer. This time around, it's taken the leash off its perspective making the move to full 3D, but in trying to do and offer more has only served to highlight its many failings and
managed to overstayed its welcome.
I say it's taken the leash off its perspective, but actually it's only done so to prove it's really just a big, sleepy dog with no fangs that frequently trips over its own feet and occasionally sh*ts itself. Only on a small handful of the 166 levels does the extra added camera movement prove necessary to solve the puzzle. Otherwise, you can keep it in its default position for the majority of the game.
But it does now make the controls more awkward, as the right mouse button used to move the camera, is also used to interact with a certain propelling, green block, the result being you'll try to click on the block either in place or whilst in motion, and will end up moving the camera around instead. A couple of times during one or two puzzles would have been forgivable, but being such a regular occurance gradually wears you down. But that's far from the only frustration.
The biggest problem I had with the game was the actual physics... quite a big issue in a physics-based puzzle game. For the simpler puzzles, it's really not a problem and there's such a comfortable margin for error that it really doesn't matter. But the more ambitious or fiddly some of the puzzle layouts get, the more it shows just how ill-suited the engine is for it. Either that or how poor the design is that doesn't accommodate for that fact.
In some of the later stages it really is so inconsistant that it's honestly a 50-50 chance as to what result the exact same action will produce. You click on a green block to send it flying and push another block across a small gap, and half the time it will clear it smooth as butter, and the other half it will get jammed in the gap and force you to retry the stage. I lost track of the amount of time I spent replaying sections because of this happening over and over.
Oh, and as an extra added bonus, the save function is somewhat broken and continuing your game will force you to replay the last stage you completed, rather than starting you on the last stage you unlocked. Yay.
I was so close to giving this a Yes/thumbs up recommendation just because of how minor and cheap it is, as well as how much content you get for the asking price (2-3 hours of play), and is why it almost begs for a Neutral recommendation. But since that's not an option, and the more I thought about it, the more I realised that for the majority of the game I was either asleep due to how easy the stages are, or greatly frustrated at feeling like some stages were cleared out of pure, dumb luck thanks to the wonky physics. Having more of something that isn't really all that great in the first place is hardly a saving grace, and given that your own personal time is such a valuable commodity worth considering, I can't help but feel as though this game is just more trouble than it's worth.

This game seems pretty good at first glance. I couldn't be more disapointed.
The thing they seem the most proud of - HoS being cross-platform - is the biggest problem. PC controls are terrible, everything from navigating the main menu and in-game interface to actualy controling your hero is annoying and okward af but you still get HUGE advantage over mobile players which results in effortless kills.
Matchmaking is non-existant: 70% of games are just 1st day newbs mainly on mobile phones so after few games when you learn the basics of the game and some hero mechanics the game becomes very dull and unchallenging - untill you end up in one of remaining 30% of matchups - agains a lvl 100+ players. Yes, you heard me - lvl100. I'll get there soon.
Growing your account is done with in-game gold - you use it to purchase heroes, upgrade heroes (thought it's a good idea actualy - untill I got matched against a lvl100) and upgrade hero items. The gold is rather slow to farm while everything is costly to upgrade. You can always buy the gold with $$, it's not that expensive but that depends on where you live really - I'd estimate you can buy a week of gold farming with $20. It wouldn't be a big deal if you could maintain at least one hero and itemset at max lvl but oooh nooo, noo, forget about it - without buying additional gold that's possible.
Now what the upgrades actualy do? For hero you can choose to upgrade DMG, Defense, Movement and Ultimate cooldown, for items you upgrade their stats 1% per lvl. So when you face a lvl 100 opponent he is not only much more experianced with game and hero mechanics - he simply has much, much better stats right from the start of the game. Most high levels are being♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ they always play to win just destroying the poor newbs even under turrets. Game has built in emote system - they will rub those in your face after every kill like they actualy made a "play" while the reality is what it is.
They claim it's a highly team oriented game.... Doh! It's a MOBA, what else could it be? Do you know why they think theirs is more team oriented than others? All the income you make is shared with all your team. Interesting, you might think. Well, all the newb / intentional feeding is given to entire enemy team, not just one hero so....
The chat system is terrible and the emotes aren't enough to communicate, at least not in a team based game haha - all you can say (excluding stupid "lols" and "ouch" and "oh no!s") is "attack", "defend" and "follow me". You can't even ping it precisely on the map - it just displays a stupid emote. Even old fashined chat is just bad - there's no way to view chat history, chat bubbles appear for only like 1-2s and they dissapear forever. You can't even start typing by pressing a key, no. You have to open that stupid emotes menu and select chat in there AND THEN click in the text field to start typing.
To avoid being so negative I'll name some advantages but there are not so many.
Most heroes are actualy unique so that's a big plus for not just copy pasting like most mobile MOBAs do.
Server connection feels stable and pings are pretty low (was around 50-70ms for me, Im based in central Europe).
Eventhough controls are terrible, hero movements and skill animations are pretty smooth - this game is supposed to be played on a gamepad anyway.
Players can join to ongoing games replacing leavers and afkers - I like the idea but... Well, there's no team balance mechanics, it didnt seem like system would consider players' hero level, rank and such. Oh, btw - after 3 days of right clicking 1st day newbs I was rewarded with Diamond rank which is 2nd highest - no challange at all.
In general a good idea but bad execution. STAY AWAY as it's a typical capital letters, yelling in your face "NOT PAY TO WIN" mobile game that requires paying to keep up with others.

Excellent little game. "Little" probably isn't applicable to it though, I know it's going to gobble up a hefty, and good, amount of hours.
Everything about it is charming from the art style, character design, great voice overs and acting, and sound effects. It gives me Torchlight vibes though is certainly its own unique style and take on the generic DnD-esque fantasy setting. I was actually pretty surprised at the voice acting between all the different monsters and even other fellow prisoners. Quite good.
The way the dungeons are setup and the way enemies work gives the game a fantastic rat-race sort of feel. The feely feel that feels... Like capturing the enemy intelligence on 2Fort as a Scout and making a make-or-break dash out of the enemy base feel. Except you're a scruffy peasant being chased by a pack of angry Orcs  through trap-laden halls while also trying to remember if the invincible rock golem you escaped from earlier is up ahead and to the left or just around the next corner.
[del]Now's a good time to mention there is no minimap or anything. You are, after all, a dingy little prisoner anyways. Thankfully you have a compass for this sort of thing in your HUD, and while it makes keeping track of where health potions and the like are sitting around that you'll probably need to run back to later as you run into more enemies, it adds to the atmosphere of this game.[/del] As noted below in the comments, there IS a minimap (Yay!)! You can't carry supplies around with you: You have two hands that are occupied by your sword and shield, that's it. The rest you have to scavenge for when you need it, which makes the rat-race feeling all the more dreadful when you're racing through halls trying to find that plate of waffles tucked away in a storage room while fleeing a monstrous skeletal ogre.
The gameplay itself is surprisingly good for its simplicity. You're limited to an interact key, movement, a sprint key, a jump key, LMB to attack and RMB to block with your shield, and that's it. The spice comes from using the environment of the dungeon against your enemies, whether it's thinning out a throng of Orcs chasing you by leading them down a trap-laden hallway or steering a monstrous rock golem towards a pack of skeletons up ahead and making your escape in the ensuing chaos. My only complaint here is that knocking over iron fire pits or even large torches takes some doing; a kick key or something would be pretty handy. In the meantime I don't mind that it makes chases even more frantic while you struggle to knock over a fire pit with your sword to block a doorway soon to be teeming with prison guards.
Apart from that, you can also use gold collected from slain enemies, treasures you've found, or from smacking boxes around, and place them in shrines in the dungeon. There's one that demands 15 gold per sacrifice and another that wants 100: Both generate a random buff or affect on your character. So far there's quite a large range of buffs these shrines give you, which range from faster sprint to taking less damage to making enemies bleed when you attack or an attack bonus against specific monsters, etc. It's a good feeling after you've cleared out a dungeon to empty your pockets into a shrine and watch the buffs and affects pile up (Getting a dup buff also stacks it which is great).
And finally,
. As aforementioned there's a number of reasons replaying won't get old, though I would like to add that, as you probably know, the dungeons do change upon replayability. There are specific enemies/events on each dungeon level, though the layout and the types/number/placement of enemies changes DRASTICALLY between each playthrough. The devs weren't kidding when they stressed the dungeon layout changing. ALSO NOTE that when you replay after dying you can choose to start at a specific dungeon level, though your buffs from your last life don't carry over. So it makes permadeath softer in a way which is nice; I'm more prone from starting as an underdog than building my tower of cards before reaching the dungeon I'm stuck on.
- Great voice overs/acting and sound effects: Fantastic atmosphere
- Charming and distinct art style
- Simple gameplay mechanics with surprising depth
- Just downright fun; it'll pay you back in full with gameplay hours
- No "kick" attack/mechanic (Makes triggering some dungeon elements hard)
- No sneaking mechanic whatsoever (Though given how cramped the dungeons are there isn't really use for one, though there are some instances this would be nice to have)
I bought the game for about $2.50 in a bundle sale, though I'd recommend it at full price. It's an honestly fun game with its own charm that will definitely pay back in hours of gameplay.

Unfortunatley, a lot of people who would love this game, are not going to persist past the first level. Which is a real shame, because those that do, quickly fall in love with this playful, whimsical dungeon escape simulator. For those unfamiliar with the game, it follows the hero's attempt to escape the dungeon, starting with absolultely no offensive or defensive abilities, apart from the fleetness of your feet. True, avoiding the dungeon's denizons at first is essential, but once armed, it becomes a joyful physics  heavy journey of destruction to freedom. You need to milk each level for all it's worth, in order to gain enough gold for upgrades though,  as without these, you will succumb to permadeath all to quickly. A little bit of luck will grant you the right buffs however, then you can relax and enjoy the ensuing carnage.
Punctuating the journey at various points are events which offer a  humorous welcome  break from the endless death and skeleton macaroni soup that you are helping to create. The easter eggs offer truly LOL moments, and you can see the care with which the developers have exercised in crafting a thoroughly entertaining experience.
It certainly will take you a while to work out the best system for assaulting the dungeon, and you really need to overcome the initial feeling of hopelessness, but it resolves into such a clever game that really needs to be completed. Well played PhiGames, well played.

Not specific ones that are setpieces for the level. I hope someday to have a worthy successor to this fantastic game.

This review will get hated by the Factorio community but here we go:
Even though I like the game, I would not recommend it in its current state for the current ($20) price.
Don't get fooled by those with 500h in that keep screaming this has major replay-ability, because I am sure that it doesn't to a lot of people. There isn't actually a great variety in what you can produce, every game will involve the same steps en calculations. Sure there are small parts (mostly logistics) you can optimize and change. But the whole process from ores to rockets is a simple and static math problem concerning ratios. (Solved in a few min with a Excell sheet etc.)
So IMHO it's not worth the $20 if you look at the game CONTENT wise. Games like Prison Architect hold much better value in that sense.
The game is fun, just don't get all hyped up cause the forum is full of people shouting this is worth so much more because they have 500+ hours in this. Keep in mind that the community exist mostly of people who have already paid the $20, this is also true for the reviews.

I love Fight the Dragon!  I didn't think I would like it as much as I do.  I became addicted right away.  With almost all the levels being user created there is a ton of creative adventures to go on. Creating adventures is quite simple and intuitive.  I made my first level (Rendlehelm Forest) within a few hours and it has some pretty cool features and looks pretty good.  The Steam Workshop items add a lot of options to the character customization, and I expect the options will get even better as more people make more complex pieces.
The gameplay is very fun.  Old-school hack & slash with light RPG elements mixed in.  It is so simple yet so fun that I can play this with my young son, and my wife enjoys it too!  It's complex enough though, that I could easily play this with my gamer friends for hours and have a blast.
The dragon is a lot of fun to fight too.  At first it seemed hopeless because the dragon is so powerful and you do so little damage.  However, as you level up and get more powerful you see the health finally start coming off in larger chuncks and you really feel like you are accomplishing something.  It's also really cool that it starts at 1,000,000 hitpoints and the damage done to it persists.  Talk about epic battle!  I'll be fighting this dragon for months.
I highly recommend this game!  The more people that play and contribute the better it gets!

An excellent game that just keeps getting better.
I have been playing this game with friends online for months now.  The games last about an hour, and are filled with cute, furry animals, backstabbing galore, and engaging strategy.  While frustrations can arise and luck can turn decidedly against you, we've found that even characters who suffer crippling misfortune early on can (and often do) bounce back to take the win.  However, you need to know your strategy, because a bad choice can lose it for you even when you are ahead.
The nature of the game and relatively short duration of the matches allows players who normally have trouble with competatively backstabby games to enjoy this, making it a game we all have fun with.
The multiple paths to victory make for a lot of fun.  You always have to keep an eye on the other player's progress towards other victory types even as you pursue the one you have chosen, and you often find yourself trying to keep as many paths open to you as you can.
The game is cute as hell.  The characters are adorable.  And the fights are a lot of fun.  (I'll admit, I have spent an unreasonable extra amount on skins for characters and dice just to customize. The mechanics are fairly weird. A player may play one card (move OR attack OR other) on one of his characters, then the enemy does the same. Repeat until both can't do any moves any more (because they don't have moves left and the enemy is not in range for any attacks). As soon as a stalemate is reached and both players "pass" a new turn will begin (and you get new cards). If just one player has to pass, then the other can still burn through all his cards until he is done (and with the way movement is handled this happens a lot (more often to the enemy, but that's boring too)).
And since moves are cards, with the way it works right now, you are really trying NOT to move up to the enemy and let them come to you, so that you can first strike.
If your three guys fight against one enemy, then by the time all three had a chance to do something, the other guy will have had three actions. Right in one of the first fights there is an enemy who covers the ground in acid. And you have no way of getting out of it. He uses an aoe spell that puts more than one of your guys into acid. And if you use a move action to get out of the acid he just uses his skill on you again (because if it is 3v1, then he moves three times as much as you do). The fight is still very winnable. It just feels idiotic.

After finishing the story, all the side missions and getting 100% on this game, my opinion on this game is neutral. If I compared this to Ghost Warrior 2, it has major improvements, still this game cant reach the level of Sniper Elite IP. On to the review.
Story:
I dont have much to say for the story, its a generic younger brother finding older brother who got captured by a secret society. I give 3 chances to guess the plot and the ending. Seriously, nothing groundbreaking.
Sound & music:
The music in this game is good, I dont if it's a Russian language or Polish, but I like it. It plays on loading screen and the main menu, its like a folk song. The sound of the gun and the sound when my shot hit the enemy are solid. But the sound of the world isnt much, because the world is empty flat boring, aside from the howling of the wolf, reindeer, footstep, pretty much is silent. The enemies also have a conversation, but most of the time are repeatable. The dialogue can be cheesy, sometimes even cringy, but for me, its not a big deal.
Gameplay:
Ghost Warrior 3 has a major overhaul from the prequel, now it has an open world, which suits the game perfectly. You can go to the highest cliff and kill the enemies one by one, or stay covered in the woods and snipe the enemies, or go straight to enemies and kill the stealthily. Gun blazing is an option too, but you will die in 4-5 shots because you only has 3 health bars. Climbing is the new trend in this game. The gun play is rock solid this time, the weapons are nice, some has silencer, some dont. The silencer is one the consumables, each time you shoot, it will wear the silencer bit by bit, you can fix it by using silencer fixer. Stealth system is here, similar to Far Cry. For the weapons, beside sniper rifles, you also has secondary weapons and sidearms which variety of choices, from sawed off shotgun, automatic shotgun, magnum, ak47, machine guns etc. There are 2 bows for people who likes playing stealth, composite and curve bow, use the curve bow, its better for aiming. Consumables including frag, gas grenades, throwing knives, mines, c4. Colletibles are back, quite a lot, there are 191 POI, classic rifles (which you can see on your safehouse, but cant be used), weapons(sniper rifles, secondary rifles and sidearms) and jewelries. One of the new additions is the drone, a very neat addition. You have one drone you can use to tag enemies, spying alternate route, items, hacking cameras, hacking doors, and luring enemies. That's not all, you can customized your drones by adding gadgets, like Night vision, thermal vission, small/medium/big battery, camouflage, etc. Aside from collectibles, there are also wanted targets, killing all these wanted targets will reward with an achievement only.
The world:
The world of Ghost Warrior 3 is pretty, especially at dawn and dusk. Sadly, this beautiful world is empty, there are no civilians or enemies on street, this makes the game lack of immersion. If you are a person who likes going from place to place by vehicles or foot, you are going to have a boring time.In Far Cry I love using vehicles or running by foot to the objectives, but in this game, after playing it for the first 13 hours, I started using fast travel. Cause there is nothing to see on the road, sure the scenery are gorgeous, but lack of civilians, enemies or animals, it will grow old. There are several animals that I encountered, deer, cow, dogs, cats and wolf. Wolves and deers are abundance, they stretch out thin, but they never cross the road, they only stay in the wood.
Optimization:
Got stutters and crashes, 5 crashes and some stutters, I play in 1080p, very high setting (i5-6600K, 16GB & GTX1070). Playing in borderless window and enable vsync help a bit with the stutter. One thing that I dont understand is why there is no option to turn off the HUD, why do you tied the option to turn off HUD with difficulty.
Conclusion:
I bought this on sale, happy with my purchase. You have 3 options, get it now, wait for sale, or stay away. I say, Wait For Sale. The content is not enough, I dont think collectibles can be justified as content, there are only 16 side missions spread across the 3 maps, 26 main mission which can be completed under 15 hours, stutters and crashes. Thanks for reading, whether you agree or not with my review, please be a civilized person.

It has been hard for me to find good Roguelikes that can capture my attention as much as The Binding of Isaac has. Most of the time I am left with a sense of wanting or feel like the game doesn't have enough to it to make me want to play it more, But TinyKeep is one that I plan to play for quite a while.
It's biggest advantage is it procedurally generated environments, which I feel most in not all Roguelikes need. While each level of the dungeon has the same ultimate goal, the traps, rooms and enemies are always different. One playthrough might have you dealing with more archers, while hte next could have you dealing with more barabrians. And that's just the tip of the iceburg!
The game boasts a unique leveling system, or at least unique in the sense that you don't really gain XP. instead, certain enemies and environment items from coins which you can exchange for enhancements to your character at specific alters placed in the map. There's always one at the end of hte dungeon, so you can save up until you get to it, or you can find the secondary one hidden somewhere. The second one costs much more in coin, but usually gives much better buffs because of it.
It's not extrememly challenging when you're faced with only a few opponents, but soon more traps nad enemies appear, giving you less room to run, and that's when it gets tense and fun. I'd highly reccomend this to anyone who likes The Binding of Isaac or any other good Roguelike and wants to try something new.

Block, move backwards, counter attack, repeat until dead or victorious. You get knocked out of attack animations by taking damage, and if you get swarmed by enemies - which happens every now and then - there’s not much you can do beyond take it and die. You can run away, but if you’re surrounded you’re going to be taking a lot of hits regardless. Also you inexplicably run at about half speed when you’re on fire.
It’s frustrating in more ways than Rogue-likes usually are. It’s fairly fun to play when the enemies are light and you can plan your routes, leading them onto traps and so on. But when melee combat is a necessity, things take a turn for the worse. You get stuck on objects that litter each room, which you then have to jump over, and you can’t block while jumping, obviously. It’s all just a bit of a hassle which, to be fair, I imagine escaping from a keep would be. That said, I like the style, and could potentially see TinyKeep as a light introduction to the genre but it is hard to recommend to veterans.

Factorio's simple design and graphics make it possible to run on practically any PC that boots up, and they did an excellent job with it too. Valiant Hearts: The Great War/Soldats Inconnus: Mémoires de la Grande Guerre is a game developed and published by Ubisoft Entertainment and goes through an era of history not really discussed about in this type of medium which is World War I
Valiant Hearts: The Great War takes you on a journey through the intertwined lives of characters through the first world war. As the player progresses through the story, the game captures some of the ills fated for those who lived through the war and how it affected the lives of individuals. The music at times is a bit hokey, but overall the audio in game helps. Game play is fairly simple and nothing is too complicated. Anyone should be able to enjoy this game
The story in Valiant Hearts: The Great War has been exquisitely crafted to bring together the lives of several individuals including one who cannot truly speak for themselves
The gameplay is super simple, nothing to it. Easy to play though sometimes you're not entirely sure what the game wants from you. This didn't really happen till much closer to the end though. Overall the music is great
The comicbook style of the game is very well done, with backgrounds and details lending to the overall immersion into the story by the player. Contrasts in some scenes help express a complicated feeling that you grasp instantly, instead of having to read words to get what is being communicated
Valiant Hearts: The Great War is definitely worth the play and the money. Shame about the forced DRM of Uplay but hey what do you expect, it's Ubisoft!

It's not a bad game. It has its moments. But game developers have made some poor choices while designing this game. It starts out as a pretty fun game. But there are bugs that ruins the mood at times. It's been 2 years since the game came out and the developers still didn't care to fix them. The problem is, you wouldn't know they are bugs. You would think you have to do something, like solve a puzzle in order to advance. After trying for hours when you give up and then later on come back and play again you won't encounter the bug again because they occur only intermittently. Then you realize you just wasted hours trying to solve a puzzle that didn't exist.
Speaking of puzzles, I love them and this game has plenty. Many of them are quit intersting. If the game contained only puzzles I would have loved it. However, there are a lot of pointless quicktime events that are excruciating. I like playing games that needs skills. If the quicktime events tested your response time, it would be fun. But that's not what they test! The quicktime events are so poorly designed, especially in the latter half of the game, that the only way to get through them is to try them again and again till the point you remember every move. That's incredibly poor design. Quicktime events can be fun if it tests your response time. In fact they should be randomized every time so that you cannot rely on your memory. That's the correct way to incorporate quick time events in your game. But they become a chore when you have to memorize them. I reached a point where I stopped caring about some of the characters in the game because the qt events were so pointlessly hard. I was like, "Fine let him just die. I don't care anymore."
Another poor game design is that it doesn't save on all the checkpoints, only some of them. When you're playing and you die, it will start from the previous checkpoint. But if you quit and come back, it may or may not start from that checkpoint. Many times it will start a couple of checkpoitns before. Which means you have to replay levels you have already played before. And there is no way of knowing which checkpoints are saved and which aren't. I have found myself repeating so many parts because the game didn't save.
The reason it is getting such rave reviews is that because it's a WWI story and people romanticize it. And the story is pretty sentimental and most people are suckers for romanticized, sentimental war stories. Otherwise the game is like 5 on a scale of 10.
I would higly recommend you wait for a 75% off or higher sale. It's not worth the price. I regret buying it.

I do realise I have immense nostalgia for this game, so this review is biased towards those that love old school collectable and platforming games.
Short General Review: I can whole heartily say that this remake is one of the most faithful and respectful remakes I have ever played, and if you have a craving for an old-fashioned collectafon with solid platforming mechanics that has aged very well then you
to buy this!
And just to further show my appreciation I nominated this game for the test if time award!
For people (like me) that played and love the original on console its great, but it does have some little problems that (while small) are noticeable.
The first problem I have noticed was the draw distance, with large maps like 'Ship Rex' and 'Rex Marks The Spot' the opals underwater require you to be rather close for them to pop in and yet other times can be seen preloaded from miles away. As this is a collectafon this can be quite concerning as there are 300 opals and missing one can cause me 20 -30 mins of in-depth back peddling and searching.
The second problem is that some smaller levels ('like snow worries' on high platforms) can allow you to view outside of the map into a black void. This probably due to the 16 : 9 aspect ratio and these maps weren't necessarily scaled for widescreen displays.
As you can see this is a very small list of complaints, and that is because I believe that these Devs have made something truly great and worth your time! All I can say is I wish the Devs my most thanks as it has rekindled something I thought was long dead from my childhood.
Keep Up the good work guys! And if your Team would ever make a Ty 2 remake I (and this reborn fanbase) wouldn't hesitate to pick it up!

This is one of the games I wish we had the option for a neutral review, but since I feel the pros slightly outweight the cons I'll go with a positive one even with its issues.
The game itself is rather fun. Think of a Studio Ghibli movie meeting Game of Thrones. It's a board game where you and 3 other people or AI roam a beautiful board trying to complete objectives while fighting each other and the board pieces or making alliances. There's 4 ways to win a game and all of them require the King to die or get banished so you become the next King/Queen, the thing is the vast majority of games it's gonna be one of two ways, either a Kingslayer or a Prestige victory.
There's 4 clans, each of which has 3 possible heroes for you to choose, 2 if you don't have the Unsurpers DLC. Every one of them is a viable choice for competitive play and uniquely built with their strengths and weaknesses.
The game has a good enough mix of strategy and RNG. Sometimes you can find yourself in a corner because RNG screwed you in a game or ahead of the others because it favored you. Building your hero in a way that minimizes the RNG effect on you is also a core part of the game.
The queues always felt good to me. I see a lot of complaints about people waiting too long for games yet I never had to wait over 2-3mins. I don't know if it's a timezone thing but for me this never was a problem.
The real problem with the game is the stability issues. If you get disconnected in Multiplayer that's it, there's no way to rejoin the game. And more often than not this can also cause the match to completely freeze, forcing everyone to abandon a 1h+ game. And it can really freeze at any time, without anyone leaving too. In my experience this affects 25-35% of the matches I've played.
Also LoG has decided to milk their customers by going down the DLC and microtransactions route. First there was a character pack which let's say it's okay. Then a 5€ DLC that just adds 2 more color palettes for the board map. And with version 1.6 came ridiculously overpriced Hero Skins as well. At least besides the character pack everything is purely cosmetic and does not affect your game experience.
Lastly the community seems to be a rather decent one in my experience of Multiplayer. There are the occasional trolls and afk farmers but they're much more uncommon than pleasant people you meet during your matches. The problemtic thing is the AI that takes the place of someone leaving the game. They are really not the brightest ones around. They're generally quite bloodthirsty even when the odds are really stacked against them and will rush breaching the palace quite often(that's the last phase of the game).
tl;dr
Pros
-Beautiful artwork
-Balanced
-More than 1 victory type allowing you to play in different ways
-Enjoyful experience(when it works)
-Good variety of cards
Cons
-Multiplayer Freezes sometimes
-No way to reconnect in an ongoing game
-cosmetic microtransactions and DLCs
-a bit prone to RNG
-Horrendous A.I.
All in all I'd say if you enjoy board games and don't mind some RNG involved it's a good choice for you, it certainly was for me!

I promised myself that if I played 200 hours of this game, that I'd leave a review.
1st off, let me say that I personally hate the binary system steam forces you to use - you either recommend this game, or you do not.
While I do personally love Armello, I'll be the first to shove an♥♥♥♥♥♥in my face and say that this game isn't for everyone. If you hate digital board games, where people might literally spend 5 minutes on their turn, then DO NOT get this game.
But if you like outwitting your opponents (albeit there's a rather hefty component of luck involved), if you don't mind waiting for your turn, and you do like board games, Armello is for you.
I personally love the 'game-of-throne'/'redwall'-esque mechanics of the game. The artwork is second to none, and is perhaps best described as Disney-meets-anime.
As for gameplay, I love the varied victory paths available to the player. It means that no matter how cr4ppy a start you may have, you will ALWAYS have a decent chance at victory. This is precisely what makes the last few rounds of Armello so darn exciting. The heroes available to the player feel very balanced, and are all geared towards a very distinct playstyle - however, they are by no means restricted to be played in a one dimensional manner.
That being said, I do have my complaints. Suffice to say that I own a powerful gaming laptop, the incompatibility of Armello with windows 10 makes playing it like having a papercut on your♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ It's not going to stop you from getting the deed done, but it is rather unpleasant. The framerate is choppy, the game does crash occasionally, and it consumes about 40% of my 8gbs of RAM. That being said, it is a problem the devs are aware of, and I do believe that they are working on it.
Another complaint I have is the inability to reconnect into a game. For instance, should the game crash due to the aforementioned reason, it automatically counts as a defeat. And do note that the game DOES lag-out for all parties occasionally.
Overall, I do enjoy playing Armello. It's a great game. And I personally am okay with the shortcomings of it as I can imagine how difficult it must be for such a small dev team to keep this game running.

You're looking at this game because you want a modern, tactical stealth/sniping FPS. I suggest you pass this one over.
It looks like Far Cry met Sniper Elite - but in chasing both hares, catches neither.
After tweaking with settings, and trying to put up with the occasional bug (I'm not so picky that the occasional hiccup throws me) I'd just had enough.
Excessively long load times, with a mind-numbing soundtrack (no matter how ethnically accurate, it turns into droning after about 3 minutes)
-Frame rate is choppy even on high end machines, it's just poorly optimized - and often caused button inputs to be missed entirely
-Cutscenes animated straight out of 2002 graphics
-Mind Numbing Soundtrack
-Poorly tries to recreate gimmicks from Sniper Elite series, to minimal effect
-AI was unbelievably simple, often not seeing me ~20 feet away
-Open world is fairly barren, except for outposts which are surrounded on all sides by ideal sniper perches
-Character writing is shallow and bland - don't come here expecting a story
-Most of the dialogue is presented as if the protagonist is hated, or owes someone - they help him anyway, with no explanation or persuasion. They just do, often the sentence after angsting about it
-Voice acting on a not-so-subtly COD1 Zakhaev-style Big Bad sounded barely not-American
+Hey the guns are pretty cool
+In all honesty the sniping mechanics on this game are the only saving grace, but where others would be a diamond in the rough, this is more like broken glass in mud.

Not completly sure about recomend or not this game, so lets check its pros and cons:
+ Free and not pay-to-win.
+ Cross platform (Windows, Android, iOS). Actually I first played it on my android tablet (iPEGA-9700), so you can play it anywhere and anytime with a single account.
+ Matches can be quick. If you don't want to or don't have time for long matches you can play for 5min or 15 min matches.

+ Very accessible. If you're new to MOBAs or just want a lighter experience.
